200.description: Liveness only — a fixed literal. **It does not check the database or any downstream gRPC service**, so a 200 means the process is up, not that its dependencies are.

post.description:
Starts email-based registration for a **new** member. Proxies to the Yamauchi API, which creates an inactive user and emails a 6-digit OTP. Confirm it via `POST /auth/email/confirm`. Public endpoint.

If the email already belongs to a registered account, Yamauchi rejects it with `E-AUTH-020` (409). Too many requests (Yamauchi throttles OTP sends) → `E-RATE-001` (429). A Yamauchi outage surfaces as `E-EXT-001` / `E-EXT-002` (502).

429.description: Yamauchi throttled the request — retry later (E-RATE-001).

502.description: Yamauchi upstream timeout or error (E-EXT-001 / E-EXT-002).

post.description:
Starts email-based login for an **existing** member by emailing a 6-digit OTP (confirm via `POST /auth/email/confirm`). Public endpoint.

If the email is not registered → `E-AUTH-021` (404); if it belongs to a social-login account (no password/OTP flow) → `E-AUTH-022` (409). Too many requests (Yamauchi throttles OTP sends) → `E-RATE-001` (429). A Yamauchi outage surfaces as `E-EXT-001` / `E-EXT-002` (502).

429.description: Yamauchi throttled the request — retry later (E-RATE-001).

Verifies the 6-digit OTP for **both registration and login** flows and, on success, issues a fitness JWT token pair. Public endpoint.

An incorrect or expired code → `E-AUTH-023` (401). A Yamauchi outage surfaces as `E-EXT-001` / `E-EXT-002` (502).

No such address → `E-AUTH-021` (404). While the Yamauchi User API is disabled (dev) a pending address was never sent to Yamauchi, so a pending resend is a no-op 204.

post.description:
Verifies a Google/Cognito `id_token` and issues a Fitness **staff** JWT for the CRM web app. The provider is auto-detected from the token `iss` claim. On a staff member's **first** login, an `inviteToken` must accompany the id_token; it is consumed and `isFirstLogin` is returned `true`. Public endpoint.

Token verification failure → `E-AUTH-032` (401). The email not matching a staff record → `E-AUTH-033` (403); a deactivated staff → `E-AUTH-034` (403). For the invite token: not found → `E-AUTH-035` (404); already used / revoked / expired → `E-AUTH-036` / `E-AUTH-037` / `E-AUTH-038` (all 410).

200.description: Login succeeded; staff tokens issued.

403.description: Staff not registered or deactivated (E-AUTH-033 / E-AUTH-034).

410.description: Invite token already used, revoked, or expired (E-AUTH-036 / E-AUTH-037 / E-AUTH-038).

post.description:
Destroys **this terminal's** CRM Redis session — the one the bearer token was minted for (JWT `sub` + `sessionId`). A staff may hold several sessions at once, and signing out of the office PC must not sign them out on their laptop; ending someone else's session is `POST /admin/staff/{id}/sessions/revoke`, which is HQ-only.

**Idempotent** — returns 204 even if no session exists. Requires a valid staff bearer token.

Exchanges a CRM staff refresh token for a **new access + refresh pair** (rotating session — the old pair is invalidated). The Redis session is a 60-minute idle timeout (Y-13 FR-M007), re-armed by this rotation and by every CRM request: a tab idle for 60 minutes is signed out even though its refresh token has not expired. Logout kills both tokens immediately. Public endpoint — the refresh token itself is the credential.

Expired token → `E-AUTH-002`; bad signature → `E-AUTH-003`; session gone — 60 minutes idle, logged out, force-terminated or evicted by a newer login → `E-AUTH-039`; a non-CRM token → `E-AUTH-005`; staff deactivated since login → `E-AUTH-034` (403).

200.description: New staff token pair issued (isFirstLogin is always false).

401.description: Refresh token expired, invalid, or its session is gone (E-AUTH-002 / E-AUTH-003 / E-AUTH-039 / E-AUTH-005).

403.description: Staff deactivated since login (E-AUTH-034).

get.description:
The staff behind the bearer token: basic profile, role/scope, and **all 57 position permission flags**, read fresh from the position master per call (a mid-session position change shows on the next fetch — the flags are deliberately not JWT claims).

`isPositionAssigned: false` means the staff has no 職位 yet and every flag is `false` (未割当 is deny-by-default, API-070 §3.5.5) — **not** "the role's basic permissions". Render the unassigned state explicitly instead of an empty menu.

Staff record gone → `E-AUTH-033` (403); deactivated → `E-AUTH-034` (403).

200.description: The signed-in staff profile with permission flags.

401.description: Missing/invalid/expired staff JWT, or session expired / revoked (E-AUTH-002 / E-AUTH-003 / E-AUTH-039).

403.description: Staff not registered (E-AUTH-033) or deactivated (E-AUTH-034).

post.description: Mails a **one-time, 15-minute** sign-in link to the given address when (and only when) it belongs to an active staff. The response is `{ accepted: true }` either way — this public endpoint never discloses whether an email is a staff account. Issuing a new link revokes any pending one.

200.description: Accepted (whether or not the email matched a staff record).

post.summary: CRM magic link — request a sign-in link

post.description: Consumes a one-time CRM sign-in link token and issues a staff token pair. Invalid, expired, and already-used tokens all answer the same `E-AUTH-030` (401) so the endpoint leaks no token state; a deactivated staff answers `E-AUTH-034` (403). The CRM lane is separate from the MobileApp magic link (`POST /auth/magic-link/verify`), which signs a staff into the member app instead.

200.description: Token consumed; staff token pair issued.

401.description: Token invalid, expired, or already used (E-AUTH-030).

403.description: Staff deactivated (E-AUTH-034).

post.summary: CRM magic link — verify and sign in

get.description:
Verifies a first-login invitation token and returns the staff `authProvider`, `email`, and `staffName` so the CRM can render the correct login UI (Google button vs. ID/PW form). Read-only — the token is not consumed here. Public endpoint.

Token not found → `E-AUTH-035` (404); already used / revoked / expired → `E-AUTH-036` / `E-AUTH-037` / `E-AUTH-038` (all 410).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: 43-char base64url invitation token from the first-login URL.

200.description: Token valid; login UI hints returned.

400.description: Query failed schema validation — token must be 43 chars (E-VAL-001).

410.description: Invite token already used, revoked, or expired (E-AUTH-036 / E-AUTH-037 / E-AUTH-038).

post.description:
Logs in (or registers, when no account exists) a member via a social provider — `google`, `apple`, or `line`. The BFF **independently verifies** the provider ID token (signature + claims) before proxying to Yamauchi, then issues a fitness JWT token pair. Public endpoint (no bearer token).

An unknown `provider` or an empty `idToken` fails validation (`E-VAL-001`). A token that fails verification → `E-AUTH-024`. The social account having **no email** → `E-AUTH-025`; an **unverified** Google/Apple email → `E-AUTH-028`. A Yamauchi outage surfaces as `E-EXT-001` / `E-EXT-002`.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Social identity provider.

parameters.name: x-api-key
parameters.description: The app's brand key (モバイル Brand 識別設計 Layer 0): `F3-…` from the FIT365 app, `JF-…` from the JOYFIT app. Decides which brand the member is found or created under — one Yamauchi account holds a separate member per brand. Omitted ⇒ JOYFIT (the behaviour before keys existed). An unknown key is refused with `E-AUTH-040` (403).

200.description: Login successful; fitness token pair issued.

401.description: Provider ID token invalid, expired, or malformed (E-AUTH-024).

403.description: Unknown app API key (E-AUTH-040).

422.description: Social account has no email (E-AUTH-025) or email not verified by the provider (E-AUTH-028).

502.description: Yamauchi/JWKS upstream timeout or error (E-EXT-001 / E-EXT-002).

post.description:
Exchanges a valid refresh token for a **new access + refresh token pair** (rotating session). The presented refresh token is invalidated as part of the rotation. Public endpoint — the refresh token itself is the credential.

A token that is expired → `E-AUTH-002`; one with an invalid signature → `E-AUTH-003`; a token whose session no longer exists (logged out, revoked, or evicted as the least recently used device once the member is signed in on more devices than the per-member cap) → `E-AUTH-005`. Signing in on another device does NOT end this one.

200.description: New token pair issued.

400.description: Body failed schema validation — missing/empty refreshToken (E-VAL-001).

401.description: Refresh token expired, invalid, or its session no longer exists (E-AUTH-002 / E-AUTH-003 / E-AUTH-005).

post.description: Ends **this device's** session — the one named by the JWT `sessionId` claim. A member may be signed in on several devices at once (as in legacy), and the others stay signed in. The stored Yamauchi session is logged out (best-effort) only when this was the member's last device. A token minted before the `sessionId` claim existed ends every session, as logout always did. **Idempotent** — the backend never raises a business error, so a missing/already-gone session still returns 204.

Verifies a **single-use** magic link token (issued by staff via `POST /staff/magic-link`) and, on success, issues a fitness JWT token pair so the MobileApp can sign in without a password.

The token is looked up by hash; a token that is **not found, expired, or already consumed** all surface the same `E-AUTH-030` (401) to avoid leaking which case occurred. This endpoint is public (no bearer token required).

200.description: Token verified; fitness token pair issued.

400.description: Body failed schema validation — missing/empty token (E-VAL-001).

401.description: Token invalid, expired, or already used (E-AUTH-030).

post.description:
Creates a staff record plus its linked member, auto-detects the `auth_provider` from the email domain, then issues an invitation token and emails the onboarding link. **HQ-only** (system / headquarter roles).

A non-HQ caller → `E-AUTH-103` (403). A staff with the same email **and** provider already existing → `E-STF-002` (409). If Cognito user creation fails for a cognito-provider invite → `E-STF-005` (502).

**Stores** (Dev Q&A 2026-11-07): `storeIds` takes several stores for any role, managers included — the staff works in each with what its role allows, and a manager's store scope is exactly these stores. There is no separate primary store; the first id is returned as `storeId`.

201.description: Staff invited; invitation token issued.

400.description: Body failed schema validation (both or neither of stores / `fcCompanyId`, or both `storeIds` and `storeId`), or the position role does not match `role`, or a store / the FC company does not exist (`details[].field = storeIds.<i>`), or the first store has no brand, or the FC company's stores do not resolve to exactly one brand (all E-VAL-001).

403.description: Caller is not HQ (E-AUTH-103).

409.description: Duplicate staff email + provider (E-STF-002).

422.description: Email domain is not registered for CRM access (E-DMN-006).

502.description: Cognito user creation failed (E-STF-005).

post.description:
All-or-nothing: 1–50 rows sharing one role / position / affiliation / memo. Every row is domain- and duplicate-checked before any Cognito user is created, and pool users created part-way are deleted again if a later one fails. **HQ only.**

**On rejection the error body carries `details.processed[]`** — the same per-row shape as the success response, in request order, with `errorCode` set on the ONE offending row and `null` on the rest (nothing was created, so no row is `ok`). Use it to highlight the bad address instead of showing one banner for a 50-row form.

200.description: All rows created.

400.description: Schema validation, duplicate emails within the request, XOR (stores / `fcCompanyId`), an unknown store (`details[].field = storeIds.<i>`) / FC company, or an FC company spanning zero or several brands (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Caller is not HQ (E-AUTH-103).

409.description: A row collides with an existing staff email + provider (E-STF-002). `details.processed[]` names the row.

422.description: A row email domain is not registered for CRM access (E-DMN-006). `details.processed[]` names the row.

502.description: Cognito user creation failed; users created earlier in the batch were deleted again (E-STF-005). `details.processed[]` names the row.

post.description:
Revokes any outstanding invitation tokens for the staff and issues a fresh one (re-emailing the onboarding link). Only valid for staff who have **not yet completed onboarding**. **HQ-only**.

A non-HQ caller → `E-AUTH-103` (403). Unknown staff → `E-STF-001` (404). A staff who has already onboarded → `E-STF-003` (422); a deactivated staff → `E-STF-004` (422). A cognito-route address over 128 characters → `E-VAL-001` (400, `too_long`), checked before any link is revoked. Cognito failure → `E-STF-005` (502).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Staff record ID (UUID).

200.description: Re-invited; new invitation token issued.

400.description: Stored cognito-route address over 128 characters (E-VAL-001 too_long).

403.description: Caller is not HQ (E-AUTH-103).

422.description: Staff already onboarded (E-STF-003) or deactivated (E-STF-004).

502.description: Cognito user creation failed (E-STF-005).

post.description:
Deactivates the staff: revokes outstanding tokens, destroys the CRM session (their browser gets `E-AUTH-039` on the next request), disables the IdP account and withdraws the linked member. `deactivatedReason` (無効化理由) is **optional**; when sent it lands on the staff row, so the CRM can show WHY without replaying the change history. Blank or omitted → stored as `null`.

A dedicated route because deactivation is not a field edit — folding it into the partial-update verb made a destructive cascade look like editing `phone`. `PATCH /admin/staff/{id}` with `isActive: false` still works and runs the identical code, but is deprecated for this purpose.

Reversible with `POST /admin/staff/{id}/reactivate`. **HQ-only**: a non-HQ caller → `E-AUTH-103` (403). Unknown staff → `E-STF-001` (404). Deactivating the **last active system administrator** → `E-STF-007` (422).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Staff record ID (UUID).

200.description: Staff deactivated.

400.description: `deactivatedReason` over 500 characters, or an unknown body field (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Caller is not HQ (E-AUTH-103).

404.description: Staff not found (E-STF-001), or `positionId` names no position (E-STF-009).

422.description: Cannot deactivate the last system admin (E-STF-007).

post.description:
Brings a deactivated staff back: re-enables the IdP account, clears `deactivatedAt` / `deactivatedReason` and restores the linked member.

Not the exact inverse of deactivation — **no session is resurrected** (they sign in again) and **no invitation is reissued** (the account exists; a fresh invite would hand out a second credential path to it). Reactivating an already-active staff is **idempotent**, not an error — the row is left as it is, but the IdP re-enable runs again, so calling this is also how to repair a staff left with `idpSync: failed`.

The IdP step is fire-and-forget (the reactivation is saved even if it fails); read `idpSync` in the response before telling the operator the staff can sign in again.

A deactivated staff comes back only onto the route its domain uses now (§6.5.4): domain not registered / inactive → `E-DMN-006` (422); domain switched to the other auth method → `E-STF-017` (422), recover with a new invitation.

**HQ-only**: `E-AUTH-103` (403). Unknown staff → `E-STF-001` (404).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Staff record ID (UUID).

200.description: Staff reactivated (or already active).

403.description: Caller is not HQ (E-AUTH-103).

422.description: Checked only for a deactivated staff (§6.5.4): the email domain is not registered / inactive (E-DMN-006), or the domain now resolves to another authentication route than the staff's (E-STF-017) — send a new invitation (§3) instead. Nothing is saved and the IdP is not called.

get.description:
The **read side** of `POST /admin/staff/{id}/sessions/revoke`, which shipped without one: the CRM had a force-logout button and no way to tell whether there was a session to log out, so the whole flow was reported as missing.

`sessions` is an **array, newest first, with the caller's own terminal pulled to the front** (the panel renders it as 現在のセッション). It holds 0 to `maxConcurrent` entries — API-069 §3.5.1 no longer caps a staff at one terminal, and §14 anticipated the change ("if §3.5.1 is ever relaxed…"). `session` is the same data's deprecated single-object view (the newest entry), kept so the 2026-09-08 response shape keeps resolving.

`maxConcurrent` is what auth-svc actually enforces — render the footer 「同時ログインは最大3デバイスまで」 from it rather than hard-coding 3, and note the eviction rule it implies: a login past the cap silently drops the OLDEST terminal.

`lastSeenAt` is the panel's 最終アクティブ, stamped by the BFF on each request and refreshed at most once a minute, so it may trail real activity by up to 60 seconds.

`ipAddress` / `userAgent` / `authProvider` are joined off the login-history row that opened each session (`staff_login_histories.session_id` — the join §3.5.5 #4 put there for forced-logout traceability), because the session value itself holds none of them. They are `null` for sessions opened before that capture existed.

**System / Headquarter only** — same authorization and the same 404 set as the revoke, so the panel and its buttons always agree about what exists. Manager and below get `E-AUTH-103` (403).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Staff record ID (UUID).

200.description: The staff's live terminals (an empty array when nobody is signed in).

403.description: Caller is not System / Headquarter (E-AUTH-103).

get.summary: The staff's live CRM terminals — the detail screen's アクティブセッション panel

post.description:
Deletes a CRM session, so that browser gets `E-AUTH-039` on its next request and its refresh token stops working (refresh resolves the session before minting a new accessToken). Implements the Y-13 権限マトリクス row 「アクティブセッションの強制終了」.

**`sessionId` targets ONE terminal** — the panel's per-row 強制終了 button. Take the id from `GET /admin/staff/{id}/sessions`. **Omit it (or send no body) to end EVERY session the staff holds**: that is the pre-multi-session behaviour, so callers written against the old contract keep working, and it is the right answer for a lost account.

This is the **session-only** operation: it leaves the account active, unlike `PATCH /admin/staff/{id}` with `isActive: false`, which also ends every session but as a side effect of deactivating the person. Use this for a shared terminal left signed in.

**Idempotent** — a staff with no live session, or a `sessionId` whose terminal is already gone (logged out, expired, evicted by a newer login), still returns `204`. Absence is the state you asked for, not an error; it is consequently NOT a way to check whether a session exists — read the panel for that. **MobileApp sessions are out of scope**; they live in a separate key space.

**System / Headquarter only** — Manager and below get `E-AUTH-103` (403). Unknown staff → `E-STF-001` (404).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Staff record ID (UUID).

204.description: Session(s) terminated, or there was nothing to terminate.

400.description: `sessionId` is present but not a UUID, or the body carries an unknown key (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Caller is not System / Headquarter (E-AUTH-103).

get.description:
Backs the CRM "duplicate check" button (Y-01 FR-002). Resolves `auth_provider` from the email domain via the domain master, then looks for a non-deleted staff with that `(auth_provider, email)`. An unregistered domain leaves `authProvider` null and falls back to matching the address alone.

**Advisory only** — `available: true` reserves nothing; the authoritative uniqueness check is the invite-time constraint (`E-STF-002`). Soft-deleted staff are excluded, so a retired member's masked address reads as available again. **HQ-only** (the answer discloses whether an address is registered); a non-HQ caller → `E-AUTH-103` (403).

NOTE: this route only resolves because `AdminStaffController` is registered before `AdminStaffPermissionController`, whose `GET /api/v1/admin/staff/:id` would otherwise swallow it with `id="email-availability"`. Keep that order in `auth.module.ts`.

200.description: Availability result — returned for both outcomes.

403.description: Caller is not HQ (E-AUTH-103).

patch.description:
Partial update (PATCH) of staff fields. Setting `isActive: false` **deactivates** the staff — revoking tokens, destroying sessions, and withdrawing the linked member — with an optional `deactivatedReason` (無効化理由), which lands on the staff row so the CRM can show it without replaying the change history.

⚠️ **`isActive` on this route is deprecated** — use `POST /admin/staff/{id}/deactivate` and `POST /admin/staff/{id}/reactivate`, which run the identical code behind a verb that matches what they do. It keeps working so nothing breaks mid-integration.

`isActive: true` **REACTIVATES**. §6.2 originally called reactivation out of scope, which left deactivation a one-way door needing a DBA to undo; the customer asked for the way back. It is not the exact inverse: the IdP account is re-enabled and the linked member restored, but no session is resurrected (the staff signs in again) and no invitation is reissued (the account already exists — a fresh invite would hand out a second credential path to it). Reactivating an already-active staff is idempotent, not an error. **HQ-only**.

**Manager** (§6.1.1): may send `positionId` only (`null` = the same role's 未割当), for staff who share at least one store with the manager (the manager's own stores — `storeIds`, plus every store of its FC company), and only a position of the staff's current role. Any other field, a staff out of scope (FC staff included) or another role's position → `E-AUTH-103` (403), checked after the staff lookup (404 `E-STF-001`), in that order; an unknown `positionId` → `E-STF-009`.

**Clearing a field**: send `null` (an empty string is accepted as the same instruction, since a CRM text input hands back `''` where a select hands back `null`). Omitting a key leaves it untouched — the patch is applied by key presence, so `undefined` is not a value, it is an absence. `lastName` / `firstName` cannot be cleared (NOT NULL columns), and `positionId: null` un-assigns the position by parking the staff on the role's 未割当 row rather than by writing a NULL.

⚠️ **Un-assigning removes EVERY permission flag, it does not fall back to a role baseline.** 未割当 is deny-by-default (§3.5.5): the staff can still sign in and still reaches role-gated endpoints, but every flag-gated action is denied until a 職位 is assigned again. `GET /auth/crm/me` reports the state as `isPositionAssigned: false` so the CRM can say so on screen.

A caller other than HQ / manager → `E-AUTH-103` (403). Unknown staff → `E-STF-001` (404). Unknown `positionId` → `E-STF-009` (404). **Role change**: send a `positionId` of the target role (FR-005); recorded as `role_change`, applied from the next login. A role change keeps the staff's stores — since the multi-store change they are the staff's 所属店舗 for every role, and a manager's scope is those same stores (the API-070 v0.13 §6.5.5 deletion on leaving `manager` is withdrawn). **Stores**: `storeIds` replaces the whole set (see the field). Deactivating the **last active system administrator** is blocked with `E-STF-007` (422).

**Email change** (★v0.10/v0.11 §6.5.3): see the `email` field for the check order and codes. The response always carries the current `email`. For a staff who has not signed in yet, the save also re-sends the invitation to the new address — see `reinvite` in the response.

Logical delete (Y-01 FR-004): sets `deleted_at`, hides the staff from CRM lists, keeps the audit trail, and **irreversibly** overwrites the PII columns with dummy values. Distinct from deactivation (`PATCH` with `isActive: false`), which keeps the identity intact.

Sessions are then destroyed and the IdP account disabled (best-effort).

`name` is always editable. `domain` and `authProvider` are **blocked while active staff are attached** → `E-DMN-005` (409): re-pointing a domain its staff depend on would strand them outside the allowlist at their next login. Issues a single-use magic link for a staff member. Omit `staffId` for **self-issuance** (allowed for any role); provide a different `staffId` for **admin proxy** issuance, which requires an HQ role (system / headquarter).

`linkType: "mobile_app"` (default) mails the MobileApp deep link, valid 24h, verified by `POST /auth/magic-link/verify`. It needs the staff to have a linked member record — without one, `E-STF-008` (422).

`linkType: "crm_login"` mails the **CRM browser sign-in link**, valid 15 min, verified by `POST /auth/crm/magic-link/verify`. This is the Y-01 staff-detail 「CRMログイン用マジックリンク発行」 button. No member linkage is needed; instead the staff must be able to complete a CRM sign-in, so a Google-route staff (SSO is their lane) or one still 招待中 is refused with `E-STF-015` (422). Unlike the public request endpoint, this one names the reason — the operator is looking at the staff row already.

Proxy issuance by a non-HQ caller → `E-AUTH-103` (403). Unknown staff → `E-STF-001` (404); a deactivated staff → `E-STF-004` (422).

400.description: Body failed schema validation — staffId must be a UUID (E-VAL-001).

422.description: Staff deactivated (E-STF-004); missing member linkage for `mobile_app` (E-STF-008); Google-route or not-yet-onboarded staff for `crm_login` (E-STF-015).

get.description:
Returns the authenticated member's full account and profile object (API-063 §3.2.1), camel-cased from the gRPC `MemberResponse`. Yamauchi-mastered fields (name / address / gender / DOB) are served from the local cache; `facePhotoUrl` is a freshly presigned URL. `appType` is derived from `memberType` × `memberStatus`.

A withdrawn / forced-withdrawal (soft-deleted) member is treated as non-existent and yields `E-MEM-001`.

200.description: The canonical member shape. `appType` is derived from type + status and is the gate most member features check; `appMode` gates the expert-only training endpoints.

patch.description:
Partial update of the unified `/members/me` resource (API-063 §4). Send only the fields to change; at least one is required (else `E-VAL-001`). Fields fall into three groups: OTP-required (`email`, `phoneNumber`), non-OTP Yamauchi-mastered (name / kana / gender / DOB / address), and fitness-only (units, app mode, blood type, emergency contact, face photo).

**Face photo**: upload via API-006 `POST /media/presign` with `tag=member-photo`, PUT the bytes to the returned URL, then send the returned `s3Key` as `facePhotoS3Key` here. This is the only member-facing way to set it — `GET /members/verify` leaves the `noImage` state once it is set.

Changing `email` or `phoneNumber` does **not** apply immediately: it kicks off a Yamauchi OTP flow and returns **202** with `{ pendingField, message }` (confirm via the `confirm-email` / `confirm-sms` endpoints). When an OTP field is present, all other fields in the body are ignored. Non-OTP Yamauchi fields are pushed to Yamauchi **before** the local write, so an upstream failure surfaces (E-EXT-001 timeout / E-EXT-002 error / E-EXT-110 maintenance) and nothing is persisted; a duplicate email/phone there yields `E-MEM-203` / `E-MEM-204`.

**Authorization** (enforced in MemberService by member type/status): Type A active or suspended may edit any group; Type B (staff/trainer) may edit fitness-only fields but Yamauchi fields are rejected with `E-MEM-100`, and a non-active Type B yields `E-MEM-200`; Type C / vendor → `E-AUTH-100`. The App Store review account (API-064 §7.5) cannot change `email` / `phoneNumber` (`E-MEM-206`).

**Age** (APP-F-01 FR-M004 / APP-F-02 FR-M012): a `dateOfBirth` that makes the member younger today (JST) than the brand minimum enrollment age — JOYFIT 15, FIT365 16 — is refused with `E-MEM-231` 「年齢が入会条件に足りません」 before anything is written or pushed to Yamauchi; `details.minAge` is the minimum and `details.message` the line to show under the title. To judge the date when 次へ is tapped, before the face photo, use `POST /members/me/age-check`.

200.description: The full member after the update. **Only for changes that apply immediately** — an email or phone change returns 202 with a pending-change body instead.

202.description: **A different body from the 200**: the change is NOT applied yet, an OTP was sent, and `pendingField` says which field is waiting. Branch on the status before assuming you got a member object.

400.description: Body failed schema validation / no fields supplied (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Not editable for this member: Type C / vendor (E-AUTH-100), Yamauchi field on Type B (E-MEM-100), or email/phone on the App Store review account (E-MEM-206).

409.description: New email/phone already registered to a Yamauchi account (E-MEM-203 / E-MEM-204) — including the member's own: a "change" to the current email/phone is refused the same way, without contacting Yamauchi.

422.description: Non-active Type B member cannot edit (E-MEM-200), or the date of birth is under the brand minimum enrollment age (E-MEM-231).

502.description: Yamauchi User/System API timed out (E-EXT-001), or failed / refused the call in a way that is not the member's doing, e.g. the System API IP allowlist (E-EXT-002).

delete.description:
Self-service account deletion (API-063 §5). Idempotent — a second call returns `E-MEM-001`. Check order: (1) member must exist / not be soft-deleted (`E-MEM-001`); (2) the App Store review account (API-064 §7.5) cannot self-delete (`E-MEM-206`); (3) Type B (staff / trainer) and vendor accounts cannot self-delete (`E-MEM-200`); (4) an active or suspended contract, as contracts-svc holds it, blocks deletion until the member has withdrawn (`E-MEM-201`); (5) unsettled payments block deletion (`E-MEM-205`).

When eligible, the member is deleted at Yamauchi first (an upstream failure aborts before the local transaction — E-EXT-001 / E-EXT-002), then soft-deleted locally and the session is revoked.

403.description: The App Store review account cannot self-delete (E-MEM-206).

422.description: Cannot delete: staff/vendor account (E-MEM-200), active contracts (E-MEM-201), or outstanding balance (E-MEM-205).

502.description: Yamauchi self-delete unavailable or timed out (E-EXT-001 / E-EXT-002).

post.description:
APP-F-01 FR-M004 / APP-F-02 FR-M012 (会員情報の入力): call when the member taps 次へ, so the app no longer applies the age rules itself. **Nothing is saved** — the PATCH `/members/me` at 登録 saves the date (and refuses it again with the same `E-MEM-231`).

- Younger today (JST) than the brand minimum enrollment age (JOYFIT 15, FIT365 16; the brand of the signed-in account) → **422 `E-MEM-231`**: show `userMessage` 「年齢が入会条件に足りません」 as the title and `details.message` (e.g. 「このブランドへの入会は16歳以上が対象です。」) under it; the member cannot go on. `details.minAge` carries the number.
- Under 18 → **200** with `isMinor: true` and `minorNotice` 「未成年者の入会時のお願い」 (pay with a card in the guardian's name, enter the guardian as the emergency contact): show it, then let the member go on.
- Otherwise → **200** with `isMinor: false`, `minorNotice: null`.

Any signed-in member (a new sign-up is `provisional`; a linked existing member also registers).

post.description:
APP-F-02 FR-M004: call as soon as a QR is scanned on the 「連携用QR」 route, before asking for the kana name and date of birth, so a wrong or expired code is refused on the scan screen.

- Not a link QR (any other code, or one that does not decrypt) → `E-MEM-211` 「読み取れないコードです。」
- Link QR older than 300 s → `E-MEM-212` 「QRコードの有効期限が切れています。…」

Read-only and about the QR only: it says nothing about the member (that waits for the identity check in `link-existing/preview`), does not judge the calling account (whether it may link is the preview's `E-MEM-210`), counts toward no lock (FR-M006), and does **not** use the QR up — send the same `payload` to the preview and the link, before `expiresAt`.

200.description: A live link QR. Go on to the kana / date-of-birth input.

400.description: Not a link QR (E-MEM-211), link QR expired (E-MEM-212), or `payload` missing / empty / over 4096 chars (E-VAL-001).

post.summary: Check a scanned link QR right after the scan

post.description:
Read-only first step of account linking (API-066 §7, APP-F-02 v2.3 FR-M005 → FR-M007). Nothing is mutated.

**v2.3 flow — send `verificationLastNameKana` + `verificationFirstNameKana` + `verificationDateOfBirth`** (required for `member_number`). The server resolves the member from the payload, verifies the kana name (normalised on both sides) and the date of birth, and only then returns the summary. Until identity passes it reveals nothing: a wrong kana / date, an unknown member number and an unknown card are all the same `E-MEM-216`, counted for the lock. Only after identity passed: already linked → `E-MEM-215`, withdrawn → `E-MEM-219`, other brand → `E-MEM-221`, contract store not open for app linking (引き継ぎ受付 OFF) → `E-MEM-223` (the member's own current contract's store, else their primary store; never counted for the lock).

Lock (FR-M006 一時ロック): every `E-MEM-216` is counted for the calling account AND for the member number / card (across accounts). 5 failures within 30 min on either counter — the strike that reaches 5 included — answer `E-MEM-222` (423) and refuse linking for 30 min, then it lifts on its own. The account is never invalidated and its session is kept (the API-066 3-strike `E-MEM-217` invalidation is gone). A success clears both counters.

**Pre-v2.3 (deprecated)** — `nfc` / `qr` without the identity fields: the unverified preview, kept for app builds already shipped (unknown card `E-MEM-213`, no member `E-MEM-214`, linked `E-MEM-215`, withdrawn `E-MEM-219`, contract store not open `E-MEM-223`).

The caller must be `provisional` (else `E-MEM-210`). `qr` payloads that do not decrypt → `E-MEM-211`, older than 300 s → `E-MEM-212`; `deeplink` always `E-MEM-211`.

200.description: The member to confirm (member number, contract store, main contract). **Read-only — nothing is mutated** and no link is created by this step.

400.description: Body failed schema validation (E-VAL-001 — e.g. `member_number` without the kana / date of birth), payload undecryptable (E-MEM-211), or payload expired (E-MEM-212).

404.description: Pre-v2.3 only: unknown NFC card (E-MEM-213) or no member for the code (E-MEM-214). The v2.3 flow answers E-MEM-216 instead.

409.description: Target member already linked to another account (E-MEM-215) — v2.3: only after identity passed.

422.description: Identity not verified / member unknown (E-MEM-216), caller not provisional (E-MEM-210), member withdrawn (E-MEM-219), other brand (E-MEM-221), or contract store not open for app linking (E-MEM-223).

423.description: Linking temporarily locked for 30 min — this account or this member number / card reached 5 failures (E-MEM-222).

post.summary: Verify identity and preview the existing member to be linked

post.description:
Commits the link the preview showed (API-066 §8, APP-F-02 FR-M008). Send the same `linkMethod`, `payload`, kana pair and `verificationDateOfBirth` that passed the preview (a `qr` payload within its 300 s): the server verifies them again with the same rules, errors and locks as the preview, then merges the provisional account into the existing member and returns a **fresh session** (`token`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt`) with the linked member id / number / status.

**Pre-v2.3 (deprecated)** — `nfc` / `qr` with `verificationLastName` + `verificationFirstName` instead of the kana pair: exact match on the stored name and date of birth, brand checked first (`E-MEM-221`), the contract store after it (`E-MEM-223`). `member_number` always needs the kana pair.

200.description: The link is committed and a **fresh session issued** — `memberId` is now the existing member’s, not the provisional one the caller held. Replace both stored tokens before the next call.

400.description: Body failed schema validation (E-VAL-001), payload undecryptable (E-MEM-211), or payload expired (E-MEM-212).

404.description: Pre-v2.3 only: unknown NFC card (E-MEM-213) or no member for the code (E-MEM-214).

409.description: Target member already linked to another account (E-MEM-215).

422.description: Identity not verified / member unknown (E-MEM-216), caller not provisional (E-MEM-210), member withdrawn (E-MEM-219), other brand (E-MEM-221), or contract store not open for app linking (E-MEM-223).

423.description: Linking temporarily locked for 30 min — this account or this member number / card reached 5 failures (E-MEM-222).

post.summary: Verify identity and link the existing member

post.description:
For a member who cannot link in the app (照合不能・番号不明・誤った連携), after staff checked the member's ID. `yamauchiUserId` comes from §24. Refused, in order: E-MEM-215 the member already holds an account and `replace` is not set (send `replace`, or unlink first, §27) · E-MEM-235 `replace` names the account the member already holds · E-MEM-219 the member has left (APP-F-02 FR-M010) · E-MEM-234 no usable Yamauchi account with that id · E-MEM-232 the account is already linked to another member of this brand. When the account already opened this brand's app, that empty account is merged into the member and the app signs in again once. Records 連携経路 `manual`, resets the FR-M006 failure total and lifts any lock.

`replace: true` is the 紐付け直し path (APP-F-02 「連携済みの誤り」) for **staff and above** — it does not need the 連携解除 permission. The new account is checked first, then the old one is released and the new one attached in one transaction (one `app_linked` history row marked `replaced`, 「アプリと連携しました（紐付け直し）」, the old account in `replacedYamauchiUserId`); every app session of the member ends. A concurrent unlink / relink makes it lose with E-MEM-215. On a member with no account it is a plain manual link. **system / headquarter / manager / staff.**

Guard: active + not batch-started + usage-start-date not passed (BR-WTH-011) — the same chain `cancellable` publishes on the §3 list, the §5 detail and the API-093 member head-up. `comment` is mandatory (A-03 FR-002 v3).

The member returns to **the state they were in before the application** (FR-002 v3 「有効（通常）に戻る」): `active`, or `provisional` when contracts-svc says the usage start date is still ahead. §6.5 pins `provisional` flat — errata filed, because its premise (guard #3 admits nobody whose usage has started) does not hold: the guard reads the `auth.contracts` mirror, which is empty for every member enrolled through the new system, while both creation paths accept a `normal` withdrawal only from an `active` member. The flat value demoted active members out of the gate — permanently for the two populations BAT-016 cannot re-promote (legacy members with no contracts-svc contract, forced-withdrawal members held by the uncollected-amount gate).

post.description:
Brings a **currently suspended** member back before the recess `endDate`. Nothing could do this before: the member-route cancel refuses once the recess has started, and BAT-013 step 2 only fires when `endDate` arrives.

Effects in one transaction: `members.member_status` suspended → active, the application → `completed` with `endDate` moved to today (so the batch does not fire again on the original date), a status-history row stamped with the operator, and the auth contract mirror resumed. The **SoT contract is resumed on contracts-svc first** — a remote failure holds the whole release rather than leaving an active member with a suspended contract.

**復帰月 (`resumeMonth`, YYYY-MM)** — the 休会解除 sheet's month: billing restarts on its 1st. Omitted or the current JST month = the release above. A later month schedules the return instead: the recess end moves to the last day of the month before (SoT contract first, then the application), the member stays 休会中, and BAT-013 reinstates them on that day — `status` stays `active`, `contractResumed` is `false`.

post.description:
The counterpart to `/release` above, and the other half of the 休会解除 sheet. `/release` ends a recess already in progress and answers `409 E-SUS-215` on one that has not started; until now the only cancel was on the member channel (`POST /members/me/contract-change/suspension/{id}/cancel`), so an operator who filed a 休会 at the counter had no way to take it back.

Guards are the member channel's (API-093 §6C.1): the application must be `active` and its start date strictly in the future. A recess that has started must be RELEASED instead — the two verbs are not interchangeable, and each refuses the other's case.

Effects in one transaction: the application → `cancelled`, a status-history row stamped with the operator (this is what the member channel cannot record and why this endpoint exists), and the planned recess dates cleared from the contract mirror. **No contracts-svc call** — recess dates only reach the SoT when BAT-013 applies the recess on its start date, so an unstarted application has nothing to undo there. The member is notified exactly as on the member channel (N-013).

In ONE transaction the source (`{optionContractId}`) is scheduled for next-month cancel (`active → pending_cancel`, `endDate` = last day of this month — the same as `DELETE` `next_month`) and the target is added `pending_start` from the 1st of next month (the same as `POST` 翌月から). No day-prorating; both dates are server-computed (JST), so the body carries only `toOptionId`. Only an `active` monthly, non-locker option can be switched, to another monthly, non-locker option that is on the member's contract store's sales list (`GET /admin/options?storeId=…`) and whose usability allows adding it. Not idempotent: a repeat finds the source `pending_cancel` (E-OPT-006) — disable the button after submit. A `pending_start` row is not switched: cancel it (`immediate`) and add again.

post.description:
Issues an S3 presigned **PUT** URL for a single file (1 byte – 100 MB) and creates a `pending` upload session record. The `tag` selects the access level and target S3 prefix and is validated against a server-side whitelist: a format-valid but unknown tag → 400 E-MED-011, a missing/invalid tag or other body validation → 400 E-VAL-001, and a file name with no derivable extension → 400 E-MED-006.

A file larger than 100 MB → 422 E-MED-001 and a content type outside the global whitelist → 422 E-MED-002. Response: `{ uploadId, url, method, s3Key, expiresIn, requiredHeaders }`. The client then PUTs the bytes to `url` itself — the API never receives them — sending **every** header in `requiredHeaders` verbatim: they are part of the signature and S3 rejects the upload with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch without them. `s3Key` is the value to send back to whichever endpoint stores the reference (e.g. `facePhotoS3Key` on `PATCH /members/me`).

201.description: An upload ticket. PUT the bytes to `url` with the `requiredHeaders`; `s3Key` is the reference other endpoints expect. The session is created `pending` — it does not become usable until the upload completes.

400.description: Unknown tag (E-MED-011) / undeterminable extension (E-MED-006) / body validation (E-VAL-001).

422.description: File too large >100MB (E-MED-001) / content type not allowed (E-MED-002).

post.summary: Issue a presigned PUT URL for a single-file S3 upload (≤100MB)

post.description:
Issues a CloudFront signed cookie granting the authenticated actor delivery access to authenticated-tier media (`member-shared/*` + `private/*`). The request body is empty — the JWT `sub` identifies the requestor. On success three cookies (`CloudFront-Policy`, `CloudFront-Signature`, `CloudFront-Key-Pair-Id`) are returned via `Set-Cookie` (`Path=/`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=None`, `Max-Age=3600`) and the response body is empty (204).

The cookie expires after ~1 hour; the client re-calls this endpoint for a fresh cookie. `public/*` media needs no cookie.

204.description: Signed cookies set via Set-Cookie headers; empty body.

post.summary: Issue a CloudFront signed cookie for private media access

get.description: The permanent URL for a stored object; every image/video field in this API points here. Responds `302` to a short-lived signed S3 URL, so clients can cache and store this URL indefinitely and treat it as the object identity. `public/*` keys need no token. `member-shared/*` needs any valid token. `private/*` needs the uploader or a CRM staff token, except `social-avatar` / `social-media`, which any authenticated member may read (feeds render other members’ avatars and post media). Auth accepts `Authorization: Bearer`, the ADR-038 compat auth cookie, or the `exp`/`sig` capability query the read paths append — send the URL back exactly as it was returned and a plain `` / `Image.network` / `CachedNetworkImage` renders it with no headers at all. Strip the query and the same URL needs a token again.

parameters.name: exp
parameters.description: Expiry (unix seconds) of the capability minted with this URL. Present on `member-shared/*` and `private/*` URLs returned by read paths; must be sent back unchanged together with `sig`.

Partial update of the fitness profile. At least one of `heightCm`, `weightKg`, `activityLevel` must be present (empty body → 400 E-VAL-001); sending `null` for height/weight clears the stored value. Updating height affects server-side BMI derivation on subsequent API-024 records; activity level changes the PAL coefficient used by API-028.

post.description:
Creates a body composition record. The set of accepted measurement fields depends on `source` (`manual` ⊂ `healthkit`/`health_connect` ⊂ `body_planner`); supplying a field not allowed for the source → 400 E-VAL-001. BMI is server-calculated for non-`body_planner` sources when weight is present and height is known.

**`heightCm` (APP-B-01 FR-M005):** the manual-entry form carries height alongside weight, but height is a non-versioned *profile* value — sending it here overwrites `fitnessProfile.heightCm` and the new value is used for this record's BMI. It is never stored on the record: `null`/absent leaves the profile untouched. Every response — create *and* the read paths — echoes the profile height, which for past records is today's value, not the one that produced their `bmi`.

**Same-day dedup (JST):** if a record already exists for the same calendar day and `overwriteExisting` is false → 409 E-BDY-001 (the existing record is returned in the error). When `overwriteExisting` is true the existing record is updated in place.

Member-type gated: Type C / out-of-scope members are rejected with 422 E-BDY-101.

post.description:
Creates a circumference measurement session (14 optional body-part values in cm). Measurement records are immutable except for the same-day (JST) overwrite path.

**`heightCm` (APP-B-01 FR-M005):** the measurement form shows height, but height is a non-versioned *profile* value — sending it here overwrites `fitnessProfile.heightCm` rather than being stored on the session. `null`/absent leaves the profile untouched. Every response — create *and* the read paths — echoes the profile height, which for past sessions is today's value.

**Same-day dedup (JST):** if a session already exists for the same calendar day and `overwriteExisting` is false → 409 E-BDY-010. When true the existing session is updated in place.

Member-type gated: Type C / out-of-scope members are rejected with 422 E-BDY-111.

201.description: The session. All 14 parts are present, null where unmeasured, plus `heightCm` — the profile height in effect after this write. Note there is **no `updatedAt`** — sessions are immutable outside the same-day overwrite.

400.description: Body failed schema validation / invalid part value (E-VAL-001).

409.description: Same-day session already exists and overwriteExisting=false (E-BDY-010).

422.description: Member type not eligible for body measurements (E-BDY-111).

Returns the member's measurement sessions, newest first, paginated. Optional `fromDate`/`toDate` (YYYY-MM-DD, JST) filter by recorded day; `fromDate` must be ≤ `toDate` (else 400 E-VAL-001).

Member-type gated: Type C / out-of-scope members are rejected with 422 E-BDY-111.

parameters.description: Start date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD (JST). Must be ≤ toDate.

200.description: Sessions newest first. 3D-scanner sessions (`source: scanner_3d`) appear here too — they are the same table API-058 writes. `heightCm` on every item is the **current** profile height (identical across the page — height keeps no history).

get.description:
Returns the authenticated member's full social profile, including the private fields `gender` and `dateOfBirth` (read from MemberService — Yamauchi-mastered) and the live `followerCount` / `followingCount`.

The profile is **created lazily on first access** (BR-SOC-001): if none exists yet, one is generated with a random `displayName` (BR-SOC-003) and a randomly selected active preset avatar. `avatarDisplayUrl` is the resolved icon URL (custom upload or preset).

200.description: Own profile, created lazily on first access with a generated `member<6 digits>` display name. Gender/DOB are **not** visibility-gated here.

patch.description:
Partial update (PATCH semantics): send only the fields to change. Sending `null` clears a nullable field.

**Avatar (mutually exclusive)** — a profile always has exactly one avatar. Setting `avatarUrl` clears `avatarPresetId` and vice-versa. Setting both → `E-SNS-033`; clearing both → `E-SNS-034`; an unknown preset → `E-SNS-031`; an `avatarUrl` not issued by the avatar presign endpoint → `E-SNS-032`.

**Gender / DOB** are Yamauchi-mastered (API-039 §9.5): they are forwarded to MemberService (which proxies the Yamauchi API) **before** the local write, so a Yamauchi failure surfaces as `E-EXT-001` and nothing is persisted. The profile row itself only owns the visibility flags.

200.description: The full own profile after the update. `avatarUrl` and `avatarPresetId` are mutually exclusive — setting both is E-SNS-033.

422.description: Field rule violated: invalid preset (E-SNS-031), invalid avatar URL (E-SNS-032), both avatars set (E-SNS-033), no avatar left (E-SNS-034), invalid profile URL (E-SNS-035), invalid gender (E-SNS-036), invalid date of birth (E-SNS-037).

post.description:
Returns a short-lived S3 presigned **PUT** URL for uploading a custom avatar image (JPEG or PNG, ≤ 5 MB — BR-SOC-002). Flow: (1) call this endpoint, (2) `PUT` the image bytes to `presignedUrl`, (3) call `PATCH /social-profiles/me` with the returned `avatarUrl`.

Response: `{ presignedUrl, avatarUrl, expiresAt }`. Backed by the media service (`social-avatar` upload tag).

201.description: Upload ticket. PUT the file to `presignedUrl`, then send the returned `avatarUrl` (an S3 key) back on the profile PATCH.

422.description: File too large >5MB (E-SNS-038) or unsupported content type (E-SNS-039).

post.summary: Issue a presigned URL for avatar upload

get.description: Returns the catalogue of active preset avatar icons (`{ presets: [{ presetId, imageUrl, sortOrder }] }`), ordered by `sortOrder`. Use a `presetId` as `avatarPresetId` in `PATCH /social-profiles/me`.

200.description: Active presets ascending by `sortOrder`, wrapped in a `presets` key. `presetId` is the preset **code**, not its internal UUID.

post.description:
Creates a follow edge from the caller to `targetMemberId`.

- `followType: "follow"` (default) → status `active` immediately.
- `followType: "coach"` → status `pending`, awaiting the target's approval. **Requires the caller to be a trainer** (`member_type = trainer_member`), otherwise `E-SNS-046`.

Re-following someone you previously unfollowed reuses (UPSERTs) the existing edge. Returns the follow with `isMutualFollow` (always `false` for pending coach requests).

201.description: The edge. **201 either way** — read `followStatus` to tell an immediate follow (`active`) from a coach request awaiting acceptance (`pending`).

403.description: followType=coach but caller is not a trainer (E-SNS-046).

404.description: Target member not found or inactive (E-SNS-040).

409.description: Already following (active or pending) this member (E-SNS-042).

422.description: Block relationship exists (E-SNS-041) or target is the caller (E-SNS-045).

post.summary: Follow a member (regular or coach request)

patch.description: Only the **target (student)** of a `pending` coach request may act on it. `approve` moves the follow to `active`; `decline` moves it to `removed` (the row is kept, so the coach may re-request later). Acting on a follow that is not a pending coach request → `E-SNS-044`.

parameters.name: followId
parameters.description: Follow relationship ID (UUID v7).

200.description: The resolved edge — `followStatus` becomes `active` on accept or `removed` on reject. Rows are soft-cancelled, never deleted.

404.description: Follow not found or caller is not its target (E-SNS-043).

422.description: Follow is not a pending coach request (E-SNS-044).

post.description: Hides the muted member's posts from the caller's feed **without affecting the follow relationship** (BR-SOC-018). Muting is silent (the target is not notified) and may be applied even if the caller does not follow the target. Idempotent at the data layer via a unique `(muter, muted)` constraint — a duplicate returns `E-SNS-047`.

post.description: Blocks the target. Although stored directionally, the effect is **mutual** (BR-SOC-019). Runs atomically in a single transaction: every follow edge between the two members in either direction (status `active` or `pending`) is set to `removed`, and every mute in either direction is deleted, before the block row is created. A duplicate block returns `E-SNS-048`.

post.description:
Creates a post linked to one of the caller's **strength** training sessions (API-001). The session must exist and be owned by the caller (else `E-SNS-001`). One post per session — a duplicate returns `E-SNS-003`. `title` defaults to "YYYY/MM/DD トレーニング" from the session date; `recordedAt` defaults to the session end time. `visibility=coach_and_self` requires the caller to have an active coach (else `E-SNS-002`). A computed training summary (duration / volume / sets) is snapshotted onto the post; media is attached by sending the `s3Key`s of files you already uploaded.

**Upload flow (single agreed flow): presign → PUT → create.** `POST /api/v1/media/presign` with tag `social-media` → `PUT` the bytes to the returned URL with the `requiredHeaders` it names → send the returned `s3Key`s as `mediaKeys` here. At most 3 images and 1 video.

The post-scoped `POST /social-posts/{postId}/media/presigned-urls` (API-034 §9) still works and is the reverse order — it creates the media row when the URL is issued, so a post can end up pointing at objects that were never uploaded. Prefer `mediaKeys`.

201.description: The post, including any `media` attached from `mediaKeys` (empty when none were sent). `trainingSummary` is derived on read, so `totalCalories` is always null and `prCount` always 0.

403.description: Member type not eligible for social features — Type C (E-AUTH-100).

404.description: Training session not found or not owned by caller (E-SNS-001).

409.description: A post already exists for this training session (E-SNS-003).

get.description: Cursor-paginated, newest-first feed (keyset on createdAt). Includes posts from followed members (`everyone` / `followers_only`), public `everyone` posts from non-followed members (discovery), and `coach_and_self` posts of members the caller coaches. post.description:
The single POST a gate terminal makes per scan. The device type sets the direction and the member's gate state (last unpaired entry ≤24h = inside) decides: an `entry_gate` checks in a member who is outside (inside → `denied_duplicate`; pending companion invitation → companion_entry; else entry) and runs the 5-guard chain (blacklist → delinquency → family-in-use → manual gate-stop → contract validity; ④/⑤ skipped for companions); an `exit_gate` checks out a member who is inside, unconditionally (outside → `denied_other`, detail `not_inside`). Writes the audit log row and dispatches the relay unlock post-COMMIT.

**Member denials are 200 OK** with `decision: "denied"` + `denialReasonCode` — HTTP errors are device-side faults only. Auth = `X-Device-Secret` (per-controller shared secret), NOT a Fitness JWT — a Bearer token here is rejected (E-AUTH-090).

**Idempotency (§3.7):** the same `X-Idempotency-Key` from the same device within 60 s returns the first response (denials included) without judging, logging or unlocking again. The same key with a different scan body or secret, or while the first call is still running after 4.5 s, is 409 E-AUTH-094. Errors are not cached.

Read only when GATE_TABLET_MTLS_ENABLED=true; the tablet is then identified by the certificate id and the three device headers are not needed.

put.description:
All-state PUT: the whole rule is three fields and every call carries all of them (idempotent). `isMainContractRequired` toggles the main-contract axis; `allowedContractTypes` (`[]` = any type) narrows it to an active main contract of ANY listed type; `allowedServiceTypes` (`[]` = axis off) requires an active option of ANY listed service type, billing-type-agnostic (a live monthly option is used before a per-use ticket; at most one ticket is spent). At run time the two axes are OR — satisfying either allows the device.

Any contract type is accepted on any brand's store (no brand check — E-02 Bug-No10). The single `allowedContractType` (`null` = any) is deprecated but still accepted in place of the array.

Rejected: both axes off, contract types with the main axis off, or both contract keys at once (E-VAL-001); a gateStop field on a non-`entry_gate` device (E-DEV-007).

A live monthly option is used before a ticket; a ticket is used when the answer is true (never for `is_test`). The same `request_id` again answers the first result. post.description:
Creates a multi-line refund application in `pending_approval`. **staff and up.**

The refund unit is the billing **item**, because tax rates differ per line. Each line is validated server-side, in this order (v0.14.5): every line on ONE billing (else 409 E-REF-018 — split per billing); the billing `confirmed`, collected and with a successful payment (else E-REF-011); each amount within the BR-REF-003 remainder (E-REF-005): item amount minus what OTHER applications hold — `pending_approval`, or `approved` whose refund is not `failed` — and the total within the billing-level cap (§13.3: what was collected for the billing — SBPS: the source payment's allocation — minus other applications' holds; E-REF-005 with `details[].field = lines`); an SBPS source payment older than 90 days → E-REF-007. Rejected / cancelled / expired applications and failed refunds release their hold. Re-checked under a billings lock in the create TX. Use API-114 `header.refundableAmount` / `items[].refundableAmount` before submit.

The application's `storeId` is the billing store, not the applicant's (v0.14). The source payment (§13.2 — latest paid_at successful payment) gives the variant: `sbps_void` only when the total equals the whole SBPS payment and nothing else is held on the billing, else `sbps_partial_refund`. E-REF-017 / E-REF-012 can no longer occur (one billing = one store = one source payment).

`approverLevel` is derived one level above the applicant (staff→manager, manager→headquarter, headquarter→system) and cannot be set by the caller.

Store scope (§1.1): every line's billing must be in the caller's store scope (manager = `staff_stores`, staff = own stores incl. FC-company stores; HQ/system unconstrained), else 403 E-AUTH-101.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional UUIDv4 (malformed → 400 E-VAL-001). The same staff re-sending the key within 24 h with the same route + id + body gets the ORIGINAL response back (same status and body) and nothing runs again. Same key with a different route, id or body → 409 E-VAL-001. A re-send while the first request is still running waits up to 10 s for its result, then 409 E-VAL-001. A failed request does not keep the key. Replay store unavailable (key sent) → 503 E-SYS-001. Without the key nothing is replayed.

billingItemId.description: The refund unit (#300) — must belong to `billingId`.

refundAmount.description: Tax-included JPY; ≤ the item remainder (BR-REF-003 — API-114 `items[].refundableAmount`).

expectedMethod.description: Caller hint only; the server resolves the method (§13.2).

E-AUTH-101 (403) sits with E-REF-011 in the per-line loop. Idempotency-Key reused with a different route / id / body, or the first request is still running (E-VAL-001, `duplicate`).

post.description:
The 売上管理一覧 bulk-bar 「返金申請」. **staff and up.** One `pending_approval` application per billing, with every line that still has a refundable remainder at its full remainder, trimmed to the billing-level cap from the last sort_order back (ties: larger item id first; a line cut to 0 is not created — BR-REF-011 v0.14.5). `succeeded[].totalRefundAmount` is the total after trimming. Billings are processed in order, each in its own transaction; a billing that cannot be refunded goes to `failed[]` (E-REF-011 not confirmed / not collected / no successful payment, E-REF-005 every remainder 0 or the billing-level cap 0, E-REF-007 SBPS past 90 days) and never stops the others.

A month is included when its billing is collected, or is still owed (`totalAmount > collectedAmount`). Non-monthly (per-use) billings are excluded. When nothing qualifies the response is a bare `{}` — legacy parity, not `[]` and not a 404.

`invoiceDate` is the collection date (from the connected successful payment, JST) and is **`null` while uncollected**. This is a deliberate correction: legacy formatted an undefined date through moment and so emitted *today* for uncollected rows (§4.1). Clients must handle null.

No member-status gate: a suspended or withdrawn member can still read their own history — these are the records a departing member needs for tax purposes (§7.2, TBD-A150-MEMBER-STATUS-GATE).

get.description:
Returns the currently-effective terms documents for the brand, with per-member consent state.

**Response shape is the legacy `TermResponse[]`, NOT the API-076 §9.3 `{ items: [...] }` envelope** — deliberate, so the shipped app can move off `GET /api/v1/fitness-member/terms` by changing the path alone. The two endpoints answer identically for the same query; the legacy path stays in place for already-released builds. Consent state is projected as the legacy pair (`isAccept` = already consented, `showAgreeButton` = consent still owed), and `pdfUrl` arrives as `files[0].path`.

`brand` is uppercased server-side, so `fit365` and `FIT365` both match the brand-specific documents. Filter with either `purpose` (API-076 `terms_type`) or the legacy repeatable `type` — omit both for the full effective set (all 8 Y-04 types), which is what an enrollment screen wants (`purpose=membership` alone would drop the privacy and payment documents).

post.description:
`personalInfo` is a **top-up**, not a re-collection: send only the PII the member row is still missing, or omit the block entirely. Each field is merged over the stored row and completeness is checked on the merged result. When a required field is absent from both, the response is `422 E-ENR-001` with `details.missingFields` naming them — `GET /api/v1/members/me` returns the same fields (null = the row does not have it) if the client would rather check up front. `applicationSource` and `sbpsCustomerCode` are no longer accepted — the source is fixed to `mobile_app` (§3.4) and the card is resolved server-side from the member’s `cust_code` (ADR-039 D2).

**`termsConsents` is OPTIONAL** (API-153 §3.4 marks it required; optional until the spec owner rules). Omit it when the app records consent through `POST /api/v1/mobile/terms/consents` (API-076 §10) or the legacy `POST /api/v1/fitness-member/member-term/accept`. When sent, each `termsDocumentId` must be a consentable document (else `400 E-VAL-001`) and one consent row is recorded per entry with the application.

Validate-first submit: member status, usage-date window, plan/store/option references, age, payment readiness (card-on-file / JACCS), and blacklist match. On the auto-approve predicate (mobile_app + blacklist none + adult) it runs the contract + billing cascade and returns `approved`; otherwise `submitted` (CRM manual review).

**Locker**: a row of `selectedOptionIds` carrying `lockerSlotId` now RESERVES that slot — it flips to `in_use` and is written to `contracts.locker_slot_id` inside the same transaction as the contract, and is released again if the enrolment is compensated. Previously the field was stored on the application and otherwise ignored, so the locker was billed but never held. Idempotent via the required `Idempotency-Key` header (a replay returns the original response). NOTE: promo redemption + campaign discount are deferred (API-088/089); pricing is client-supplied (API-145); member activation is BAT-016.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Dedup key — must be a UUID.

201.description: The application receipt. **`member.memberStatus` is `active` when `usageStartDate` is today or earlier** — the member is promoted inline and can use the store immediately. For a future start date it stays `provisional` until BAT-016 promotes them on the day. `nextStep.message` is null for kinds other than `under_review`.

put.description: Full-state PUT. Any slot may carry a non-null feeOptionId (v0.15). The effective option is feeOptionId ?? (isBottomRow ? (cabinet bottomOptionId ?? optionId) : optionId). A non-null feeOptionId must be a locker fee option (category `locker_option`, or an option this slot / cabinet bills with) and active; an inactive one → 400 E-VAL-001. On an `in_use` slot the locker row is picked by the §4.2 rule (live row first, else the latest cancelled one): none → 422 E-LOC-017; filed for release (`pending_cancel`, or `cancelled` awaiting the batch) → 422 E-LOC-013. Clearing an override when the cabinet has no default for the row → 400 E-VAL-001 (re-sending null with no override → 200, nothing written). On an `in_use` slot, a PUT that would move the live row to an inactive option → 400 E-VAL-001 (§6.5 #4.6); a PUT that leaves the row unchanged is accepted. When the live row bills a different option than the new effective one: a started row (start_date ≤ today JST) is swapped in the same transaction (old row cancelled with end_date = yesterday, new row active from today); an unstarted `pending_start` row has its option re-pointed in place (start_date unchanged, no new row). The row already bills the new effective option → no contract write (only the slot feeOptionId is saved). A change that would give the main contract a second live row of that option → 409 E-LOC-014, nothing written. E-LOC-015 (fee period) does not gate this EP.

Each slot carries `startAt` / `endAt` (instants; `endAt` includes the post-buffer), `durationMinutes`, the MAX trainer buffers, `trainerNames`, `remainingCapacity` (capacity − the live bookings API-113 §6.1 #12 counts: normal only on an `additive` row, every live booking otherwise — v0.11) and `remainingTrialCapacity`. Pre-spec keys (`scheduledDate` / `startTime` / `endTime` / `capacity` / `bookedCount` / `remaining` / `fee` / trial settings, envelope `available`) are kept. A `trainer` caller sees only the slots it teaches (§6.10 Read — FR-002): its own trainer id is applied, and asking for another trainer's returns an empty page.

post.description: The rule, its trainer set and the first expansion commit in ONE transaction (each session with its trainer rows and a `created` history row). Template-derived or direct body (§6.5 #1): a template's pattern — its lesson and studio included (v0.10) — is COPIED, so later template edits never retro-change this rule. Expansion (§6.6): `until_date` and `count` in full now; `unlimited` up to today + 3 calendar months (`horizonDate`), topped up monthly by BAT-038 through the same holiday chain. Holiday chain (§6.6.1, the store's Y-02 calendar): its temporary closures, holidays (`mst_holidays`, the HQ holiday master) paired with its holiday hours (closed → skipped, open → kept; with no holiday hours the weekday decides), its regular weekly closed day — with `skipHolidays` they are skipped (a count rule still gets its full quota), without it they are generated and listed in `holidayConflictDates` (`closureDates` = the ones the store's own calendar closes). If the store calendar cannot be read the create fails with E-SYS-001 and nothing is written (the rule is never expanded without the chain). Trainer overlaps are probed for every occurrence and returned per date in `warningsByDate` — soft, nothing is skipped. Answers `{ recurrence, generatedCount, warningsByDate, holidayConflictDates }` with the pre-spec flat rule keys kept.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Optional (§3.2 — recommended on the recurrence create). A UUID, else 400 E-VAL-001 (`invalid_format`). The same caller re-sending the key to the same endpoint within 24 h gets the ORIGINAL response back — same status and body — and nothing is created, written to history or notified again; a re-send while the first request is still running waits up to 10 s for its result. The same key with a different body — or a first request still running after that wait — is 400 E-VAL-001 (`details[0].field = Idempotency-Key`, `code = duplicate`). A request that fails does not keep the key. Without the header every call creates.

post.description: `endTime` is NOT accepted — it is DERIVED from the lesson duration plus the assigned trainers' buffers (the MAX buffer_after, since the room is only free once the slowest one finishes) and then stored, so a later buffer change cannot silently move a booked session. `scheduledDate` must be today (JST) or later. A studio lesson needs a studio in the same store; body care may take one (validated and stored — v0.10); PT does not use one. Trial capacity is for studio lessons only. A published schedule needs at least one trainer (E-LSC-006). Checks run in the §6.1 order: the role / store-scope gate (403) first, then the studio, the trainer set (E-LSC-021), the brand, the capacity (E-LSC-005 / E-LSC-004), the trial rules, and the published-needs-a-trainer rule (E-LSC-006). Overlaps are returned as `warnings[]`, NOT rejections — cover shifts and back-to-back sessions are legitimate. Answers the full schedule detail.

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: Optional (§3.2 — recommended on the recurrence create). A UUID, else 400 E-VAL-001 (`invalid_format`). The same caller re-sending the key to the same endpoint within 24 h gets the ORIGINAL response back — same status and body — and nothing is created, written to history or notified again; a re-send while the first request is still running waits up to 10 s for its result. The same key with a different body — or a first request still running after that wait — is 400 E-VAL-001 (`details[0].field = Idempotency-Key`, `code = duplicate`). A request that fails does not keep the key. Without the header every call creates.

patch.description: `changeReason` is MANDATORY (422 E-LSC-022 when missing or blank) and is stored on the history row, so each event can carry its own reason. `expectedUpdatedAt` is REQUIRED (400 E-VAL-001 when missing): a stale one is 409 E-LSC-014, checked again inside the UPDATE so of two concurrent edits only one is saved. A cancelled schedule cannot be edited (E-LSC-013) — it is a record of what happened. `storeId` is immutable: an unchanged value is accepted, a different one is E-VAL-001. A changed `scheduledDate` must be a real date, today (JST) or later — the create rule (E-VAL-001). `endTime` is re-derived when `trainerIds` is sent or the lesson / start time changes, and kept otherwise (§6.1.2). `trialCapacityLimit` is saved whenever sent; the RESULTING mode + limit are checked — a mode needs a limit (`trialCapacityLimit: null` while a mode stays = 400 E-VAL-001), and an inclusive limit must fit the resulting capacity; with no mode the limit is stored null. Two guards protect commitments already made: changing the lesson in a way that flips its TYPE while bookings exist (E-LSC-015), and turning trial capacity off while trial bookings exist (E-LSC-016). `trainerIds` is a full replacement set when sent. The answer adds `affectedBookingCount` — the live bookings when the date, start time, studio or trainer set moves; the members still due to come are each sent N-029 (`changeLessonSchedule`) after commit. Re-pricing those bookings is not done here.

200.description: The updated schedule (§5.1 detail shape) with any non-fatal warnings and `affectedBookingCount`.

400.description: Body shape invalid, a missing expectedUpdatedAt, a different storeId, a changed scheduledDate that is not a real date or is before today (JST), or an invalid lesson / studio / trial combination (E-VAL-001).

403.description: E-LSC-101 (observer write; trainer on a schedule they are not assigned to, or on someone else's template/recurrence). E-LSC-100 (§6.10 #3) when a manager / staff / observer names a store outside their store scope (manager: staff_stores; staff / observer: own store, or every store of their FC company) — a list `storeId`, the dashboard / reservable-slots `storeId`, or a create body `storeId` (a recurrence from a template: the template's store). A single schedule / recurrence / template outside the scope answers its own 404 (E-LSC-001 / 002 / 003) instead; lists without a store filter are narrowed to the caller's stores. E-SYS-001 (500) when the scope cannot be read from auth-svc / contracts-svc.

409.description: Stale lock — at the read or inside the UPDATE (E-LSC-014), a smaller capacity or a new trial mode below the live bookings counted under the resulting mode — normal only for `additive`, every live booking otherwise (E-LSC-007, §6.2 #4c v0.11), lesson-type change with bookings (E-LSC-015), or trial capacity with bookings (E-LSC-016).

422.description: Cancelled schedule (E-LSC-013), missing changeReason (E-LSC-022), no trainer on a published schedule (E-LSC-006), invalid trainerIds (E-LSC-021 — `details[]` per offending `trainerIds.<index>`; an inactive trainer the schedule does not already have is refused, v0.15), or capacity outside the studio band (E-LSC-004 / E-LSC-005).

post.description: Cancels this session only, even if it came from a recurrence. `cancellationReasonCategory` is required, and `other` needs a `cancellationReason` (the free text stored on the schedule). `changeReason` — the audit reason on the history row — is mandatory too (E-LSC-022). In the same transaction the booking cascade cancels every `reserved` / `pending` booking — `cancelled_by_trainer` for the trainer-absence categories, `cancelled_by_staff` otherwise — and releases their seats; `affectedBookingCount` is how many, and each of those members is sent N-030 after commit. Refund / remaining-count restore is not done here yet. Idempotent: re-cancelling returns the schedule unchanged, writes no history and cascades nothing (`affectedBookingCount: 0`).

200.description: `{ schedule, affectedBookingCount }`, with the flat pre-spec schedule keys still at the top level. Idempotent — cancelling twice returns the same schedule unchanged.

400.description: Missing / unknown category, or `other` without a cancellationReason (E-VAL-001).

403.description: E-LSC-101 (observer write; trainer on a schedule they are not assigned to, or on someone else's template/recurrence).
