parameters.description: Age bucket floor. Defaults to the caller's own band.

parameters.name: sex
parameters.description: A member gender (the app's `Gender`). Defaults to no gender restriction.

200.description: The echoed filter plus up to five exercises, most-done first.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.getExercises`. The caller`s own custom movements plus the HQ masters, filtered and paged in legacy`s `{data,total,page,limit}` envelope.

Legacy paged **in memory**: it loaded every match, decorated each row with `isBookMark`, then narrowed to bookmarked, and only then sliced — so `total` counts what survived the bookmark filter. That order is kept, because reversing it changes the number the app shows.

The canonical `GET /exercises` (API-003) serves the same rows but drops `breakTime`, `unitType`, `isSystem` and the raw muscle code, and labels `equipment` into `{code, name}` — which is why this exists rather than a path swap.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Partial, case-insensitive name match.

parameters.name: mainCategory
parameters.description: Legacy `ExerciseCategoryEnum` code (`chest`, `bicepsForearms`, `legs`, `wholeBody`, `others`, …); mapped onto the v2 category axis.

parameters.name: equipment
parameters.description: Legacy `EquipmentEnum` code; mapped onto the v2 equipment axis where a v2 code exists.

parameters.name: useDevice
parameters.description: `false` = movements needing no equipment; `true` = everything else.

parameters.name: isBookMark
parameters.description: Narrow to bookmarked. Legacy only ever narrowed, never excluded.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Defaults to 20.

200.description: One page of the catalogue.

post.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.createExercise`, which posts **multipart/form-data**: every field is a part, the muscle list is a part literally named `secondaryMuscle[]`, and `image` is one binary.

The canonical `POST /exercises` (API-020) takes six discrete fields and has nowhere to put `breakTime`, `handUsageType` or the seven `isRecord*` flags, so pointing the app at it would silently drop what the member ticked on the form. Migration 018 added those columns and this is the write path that fills them.

The image is uploaded server-side (presign → `PUT` to storage) under the `exercise-image` tag, and only its key is stored — the app never handles storage itself, as in legacy. **If the upload fails the movement is not created**: legacy wrote the row and the file in one request, so a movement pointing at an object that never landed has no legacy equivalent.

Multipart parts are strings on the wire, so `breakTime` arrives as `"90"` and the flags as `"true"`; they are coerced here rather than rejected.

Answers legacy`s `{message}` and **201**. The new id is NOT in the response — legacy did not return it either, and the app`s model has only `message`.

201.description: Legacy success message.

400.description: `name` empty, `unitType` missing or one v2 has no equivalent for (`distanceDuration`, `weightDistance`), an unsupported image type, or the caller already has a movement with that name (E-VAL-001 / E-EXR-002).

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile analysis tab. The day`s confirmed sets for this movement, plus the two totals legacy computed over them.

Only confirmed sets count: legacy wrote its set rows at completion time, so every row it could see was finished, and an in-progress v2 session`s unconfirmed sets are the drafts that had no legacy equivalent.

parameters.name: exerciseId
parameters.description: Movement to report on. UUID in v2.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/DD`; defaults to today (JST).

200.description: The day`s sets and totals.

404.description: Movement not found or not visible to the caller (E-EXR-020).

get.summary: [legacy] One day`s sets for one movement

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.getExerciseById`. The Exercise Detail screen`s whole payload: the movement, its steps, its related movements and the seven `isRecord*` flags that decide which optional inputs the set-entry form offers.

The canonical `GET /exercises/{id}/detail` (API-013) cannot stand in: it translates `primary_muscle` and `equipment` into `{code, name}` label objects, has no `level`, `breakTime`, `unitType` or `isRecord*`, and shapes the description as an object of named columns rather than the positional list this screen renders.

parameters.name: exerciseId
parameters.description: Movement to read. UUID in v2.

200.description: The movement.

404.description: Movement not found, deleted, or someone else`s custom movement (E-EXR-020).

delete.description:
Legacy answers `{message}`; canonical returns 204.

API-017 delete **without the expert-mode gate** (`E-EXR-030`) — the legacy app has no mode switch. Only the caller`s own custom exercise can be deleted, as in legacy; deleting one that is already deleted succeeds again.

parameters.name: exerciseId
parameters.description: Exercise to delete. UUID in v2.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: Exercise not found or not owned by the caller (E-EXR-020).

422.description: The target is an HQ master exercise (E-EXR-040).

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `GET /v1/fitness-member/routines/chart/{routineId}`. Legacy answers a flat array of `{date, value}` where `value` is the one quantity `type` names; v2's `GET /api/v1/routines/{routineId}/stats` carries every quantity on each point instead. So this reads that once, groups its **per-session** points into legacy's buckets, and sums.

`chartRangeType` picks the window AND the bucket: `1_year` groups by month (`YYYY-MM`), every other value groups by day (`YYYY-MM-DD`). That mirrors legacy, which collapsed its own four range values to two grouping modes for this endpoint.

**`distance` is always 0, and that is parity, not a gap.** Legacy summed `distance` from aerobic records only — a strength `Trainings` row contributed a literal 0 (`utils/workout.ts` `normalizeWorkout`) — and this endpoint filters by `routineId`, which aerobic records do not have. So legacy returned zeros here too. No v2 column is missing.

`duration` is the **session** wall-clock (legacy `trainings.duration`), which is why `/stats` grew `sessionDurationSeconds`: its `totalDurationSeconds` sums per-SET durations and would report 0 for a weight-and-reps session that plainly took time. A session still in progress contributes 0 rather than dropping the bucket.

parameters.name: routineId
parameters.description: Routine ULID (legacy int).

parameters.name: chartRangeType
parameters.description: Window and bucket size. Required, as in legacy.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which quantity `value` carries.

200.description: Buckets in the window, oldest first.

400.description: `chartRangeType` or `type` missing or not one of the legacy values (E-VAL-001).

404.description: Routine not found or not owned by the caller (E-RTN-002).

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `GET /v1/fitness-member/exercises/{exerciseId}/chart`. **Five metrics per bucket, not one** — legacy returned maxWeight / maxRm / maxVolume / maxVolumeString / maxSessionVolume together, so this is not API-014's `/statistics` reshaped: that plots ONE chosen indicator and has no way to carry `maxVolumeString`, which needs the reps and weight of the specific best-volume set. training-svc grew a dedicated single-query aggregate for it instead.

`maxSessionVolume` is the field the legacy **DTO** never declared while the legacy service returned it — and the shipped app reads it (`exercise_detail_view_model.dart:74`), so it is part of the contract and a swagger-only comparison misses it.

Arithmetic is legacy's, not API-014's: volume is `reps × weight` rather than the stored `volume` column, and `maxRm` is the unrestricted `weight × 36 ÷ (37 − reps)` — API-014's `estimated1rm` limits that to 1–10 reps and the legacy chart did not. The service's docstring records both, plus the `reps = 37` division legacy answered with `Infinity`.

`chartRangeType` sets window and bucket: day for `1_week`, ISO-week start for `1_month`, first-of-month for `1_year`. `3_month` is legacy's broken case — its `getKeyByType` had no entry, so every record collapsed into one bucket keyed `undefined` — and is served here as weekly buckets over three months rather than reproducing that.

parameters.name: exerciseId
parameters.description: Exercise ULID (legacy int).

parameters.name: chartRangeType
parameters.description: Window and bucket size. Optional — legacy defaulted to `1_week`.

200.description: Buckets in the window, oldest first.

400.description: `chartRangeType` is not one of the legacy values (E-VAL-001).

404.description: Exercise not found, soft-deleted, or a custom exercise of another member (E-EXR-020).

post.description:
The one write in this group where legacy returns more than a message: `{message, id}`. The id is a **UUID** in v2.

The body is the legacy one and is TRANSLATED here (`aerobicRecordToCanonical`): `type`→`exerciseType`, `distance`→`distanceKm`, `duration`→`durationSeconds`, `recordTime`→`recordedAt`, `runningMachine`/`bikeMachine`→`machineTypeCode`, and `condition` from `great|normal|bad` to `good|neutral|poor`. Forwarding it verbatim — which this route used to do — filed every RUNNING record as a BIKE one and then 500d on a NOT NULL column.

`consumeCalories` is accepted and ignored: calories are computed from the machine`s METs and the member`s real weight.

`trainingScheduleId` IS honoured — it is what makes the planned workout on `GET /schedules` go green. It used to be dropped, on the argument that completion could be derived by matching the record`s aerobic master to the plan`s `scopeId` within the day. Those are different rows by construction: `POST /aerobics` hands the app the AE-*-UNDEFINED placeholder and the plan stores that, while this record resolves to the machine named in `runningMachine`/`bikeMachine`. training-svc now stores the link and applies legacy`s three rules: the plan must be the caller`s and be an aerobic plan (404 E-SCH-002), must not already hold a record (400 E-AER-007), and must be for the same discipline (400 E-AER-008).

201.description: Legacy message plus the new record id.

400.description: `type` is neither running nor bike, `distance`/`duration` missing or not positive (E-VAL-001), or the named plan already holds a record (E-AER-007) or is for the other discipline (E-AER-008).

404.description: `trainingScheduleId` is not an aerobic plan of the caller (E-SCH-002).

post.description:
Legacy answers `{message}` naming the **source** id, not the copy. Kept as-is.

API-017 duplicate **without the expert-mode gate** (`E-EXR-030`) — the legacy app has no mode switch. The other API-017 rules stand: the copy is named "{source} コピー", and a Type C member is capped at 3 custom exercises.

parameters.name: exerciseId
parameters.description: Exercise to copy. UUID in v2.

201.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: Exercise not found or not visible to the caller (E-EXR-020).

409.description: The caller already has a custom exercise with the copy`s name (E-EXR-014).

422.description: Type C custom-exercise limit of 3 reached (E-EXR-013).

post.description: Legacy answers `{message}`; canonical returns the bookmark row.

201.description: Legacy success message.

delete.description: Legacy answers `{message}`; canonical returns 204.

parameters.name: exerciseId
parameters.description: Bookmarked exercise. UUID in v2.

200.description: Legacy success message.

patch.description:
Legacy `UpdatePositionDto {id, newPosition}`: ONE item moves and the rest close up around it. `newPosition` is the 0-based index the item ends up at in the list `GET /folders` returned; past the end means last.

`id` may also be a **routine**: the app sends a drag inside a folder to this same path (it has no `routine-position` client), so a routine id reorders its folder`s routines as `GET /folders` lists them.

Carried out through the API-023 batch (`PATCH /api/v1/routines/reorder`): the list is renumbered 1..n and only the rows whose number changes are written, so a drop in place writes nothing and still succeeds. Answers with the legacy `{message}` for both kinds, as legacy did.

200.description: Legacy success message.

400.description: `id` missing or not a UUID, or neither one of the caller`s folders nor a routine listed in one; or `newPosition` missing or not an integer ≥ 0 (E-VAL-001).

patch.summary: [legacy] Move a folder — or a routine within its folder — to a new place in the list

put.description: Legacy answers `{message}`; canonical returns the folder.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description: Folder to update. UUID in v2.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: Folder not found or not owned by the caller.

delete.description: Legacy answers a **different** message from update — kept distinct.

parameters.name: folderId
parameters.description: Folder to delete. UUID in v2.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: Folder not found or not owned by the caller.

post.description:
Answers legacy`s `{message, id}` (`MessageResponseWithIdDto` in `backend-legacy`). **The `id` is load-bearing, not decoration**: the Record screen posts a routine, feeds the new id straight into `POST /training-schedules` as `scopeId`, then records the workout. This route used to answer `{message}` alone, and the app`s `CreateRoutineResponse.id` carries `defaultValue: 0` — so instead of failing it planned `scopeId: 0` and the finished workout was lost with no error anywhere. Nor could the app recover the id by reading: a root-level routine is not in `GET /folders`, and `GET /v1/fitness-member/routines` does not exist.

The body is the legacy one and is TRANSLATED here (`routineToCanonical`): `routineExercises`→`exercises`, `numberOfRep`/`weightKg`/`durationSeconds`→`target*`. Legacy`s `duration`, `consumeCalories`, `categoryId` and `note` have no column in v2 and are dropped rather than stored somewhere nothing reads back.

201.description: Legacy success message plus the new routine id.

400.description: A `routineExercises[]` entry has no `exerciseId`, or the service rejected the routine (E-VAL-001).

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.getRoutines` / `getRoutinesByCategory` (legacy `GET /v1/fitness-member/routines`). One page of the HQ masters (`routines.origin = official`, legacy `memberId IS NULL`) that HQ has published in CRM Y-09 — an unpublished one is not on the app — oldest first, optionally narrowed to one routine category.

The legacy envelope is kept as it was: `{data, total, hasNextPage}`, `time` / `volume` / `numberOfSet` / `achieved` always 0, `description` `""` rather than null, and `hasNextPage` = `data.length === limit` — so a full last page still answers true.

Differences: ids are UUIDs (legacy ints), `categoryId` is a routine-category UUID from `routines/list-category`, and `limit` is capped at 100 (legacy had no ceiling). `type` (`routines` | `workouts`) is accepted and, as in legacy, does not change the result.

Same masters as `GET /routines/system`, which adds the caller`s copy and plan per master but does not page.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Routine-category **UUID**. Omit for every category.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Defaults to 50 (legacy `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`); capped at 100.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Legacy `TypeQueryEnum`; accepted, ignored.

200.description: One page of HQ masters, oldest first.

get.summary: [legacy] HQ master routines, one page — routines

post.description:
Legacy answers `{routineId}` — the id of the **copy**.

The app sends two different actions through this call, and API-022 splits them:
- **the caller`s own routine** (My Routine ⋯ → 複製) — §4 duplicate: named "{source} コピー", same folder.
- **an HQ master** (系統メニュー「追加」, and the master`s detail screen) — §3 copy: keeps the master`s name and lands in the caller`s `Fit365メニュー` folder, created on first use, as legacy did — `GET /folders` has no root bucket, so a copy at root would never show in My Routine. The copy records the master as its source, which is how `GET /routines/system` reports `duplicateRoutineId`. A master the caller already copied answers **that** copy (legacy: 400 `ROUTINE_HAS_BEEN_DUPLICATED`). A master unpublished in CRM Y-09 is not on the app and is 404.

This route used to forward to the canonical `POST /routines/{id}/duplicate`, which refuses masters by spec — every master answered 404.

parameters.name: routineId
parameters.description: Routine to copy: the caller`s own, or an HQ master. UUID in v2.

201.description: Id of the copy.

404.description: Routine not found, deleted, or another member`s routine (E-RTN-002).

422.description: Type C routine limit of 3 reached (E-RTN-101), or the account cannot save routines (E-RTN-100).

put.description:
Legacy answers `{message}` naming the routine id. Same body translation as `POST /routines` — the app sends this one through the identical `RoutineMapper.mapToModel`, so it had the identical defect.

Sending `routineExercises` replaces the movement list wholesale, as canonical does. `folderId` is only forwarded when the caller actually sent the key: omitted leaves the folder alone, `null`/`""` moves the routine to root.

parameters.name: routineId
parameters.description: Routine to update. UUID in v2.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: Routine not found or not owned by the caller.

delete.description: Legacy answers `{message}` naming the routine id.

parameters.name: routineId
parameters.description: Routine to delete. UUID in v2.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: Routine not found or not owned by the caller.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `RoutinesApiClient.getRoutineDetail`. The routine, its movements with the WHOLE exercise embedded, each movement`s template sets, and what the member actually did in each slot last time they ran it.

The canonical `GET /routines/{id}` cannot stand in. It is not only missing fields: the app declares `routineExercises[].exercise` a **required** object and the canonical serializer emits flat `exerciseId`/`exerciseName` with no nested object at all, so the screen throws rather than rendering a gap. It also labels `exerciseType` into `{code, name}` where the app wants the bare legacy enum.

**One deliberate deviation from legacy, and it is a fix:** legacy looked the routine up by id alone, so any member could read any other member`s routine. This applies the v2 rule instead — your own routine or a published HQ master; someone else`s private routine, and a master unpublished in CRM Y-09, is 404.

See the response schema for the three fields v2 has no source for (`note`, `gif`, `lastDistanceMeters`) and for how the last-run values are matched.

parameters.name: routineId
parameters.description: Routine to read. UUID in v2.

200.description: The routine.

404.description: Routine not found, deleted, or someone else`s private routine (E-RTN-002).

get.summary: [legacy] Routine detail — the Record screen`s payload

post.description: A goal set less than 7 days ago is edited in place; an older one is closed the day before the new one starts, so the previous week`s target stays on record. When the member has `isWeeklyRepeatGoal` on, the goal is stored with **no end date** — that is how legacy expresses "carry this target forward until it is replaced".

200.description: Legacy success message.

400.description: `startDate` not before `endDate` (DATE_INVALID), or a malformed field.

post.summary: [legacy] Set one training goal for the week

post.description: The Home screen`s three bars (kcal / kg / km) are set in one call. Written in a single transaction — a partial write would show a new kcal goal beside last week`s km goal.

200.description: Legacy success message.

400.description: Empty `weeklyGoals`, or an entry that fails the same rules as `/create`.

post.summary: [legacy] Set several training goals at once

post.description: `goalType` and `unit` are set server-side (body / kg) — the client sends neither. Unlike the other two writes this one answers with the **stored row**, which is what legacy did. Re-posting the same `startDate` edits that goal rather than stacking a second one.

200.description: The upserted goal.

400.description: `startDate` in the past (START_DATE_INVALID) or `endDate` not after it (DATE_INVALID).

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `EntriesApiClient.getLastEntry`, which drives the Home reminder dialog.

**Not an alias of `GET /api/v1/members/me/entries/latest`.** That one answers "the newest entry"; this one answers "the most recent visit that is missing a half", which is a different question and the only one the popup can use: the dialog fires when **exactly one** of `entryTime` / `exitTime` is set, so replying with the latest entry and a null `exitTime` would claim "check-out not confirmed" on every app launch.

Legacy kept one row per visit; v2 keeps gate **events**, so gate-svc pairs each `exit` with the nearest older `entry` and then applies legacy's four branches — including returning **null** when the newest visit is an open entry and the one before it closed cleanly, i.e. the member is inside right now and there is nothing to nag about.

The columns legacy's Yamauchi import filled (`entrySeq`, `businessMonth`, `ageCode`, …) have no v2 source and are returned as **null** rather than dropped, so the shape stays legacy's. `companion_entry` is excluded — that is someone else walking in on the member's authorisation.

200.description: The visit, or **`null`** when there is nothing to report (never entered, or currently inside).

get.summary: [legacy] The visit the reminder popup asks about — entries/previous-entry

get.description: The three numbers the weight-progress chart plots. `currentWeight` is the latest weighing at or before `date`; `startWeight` is the latest one **before the goal started**, which is the baseline the chart measures against. Both fall back to the weight on the fitness profile when the member has never used a scale — legacy fell back to their counseling answer, which is the same number from the same person — and to `null` after that. **The goal is returned even when the weights cannot be read at all**: a Type C (pre-enrolment) member is refused by the body-record service, and legacy still showed them the target they had set.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/DD`; defaults to today (JST).

200.description: Goal plus the two weights. `goal` is `{}` when none is set.

get.description: Seven daily buckets from the goal`s anchor weekday. What a bucket counts depends on `unit`: `kcal` sums training **and** aerobic, `kg` is training volume only, `km` is aerobic distance only. `unit` defaults to `kcal`, as legacy`s aggregation did.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/DD`; defaults to today (JST).

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Defaults to `kcal`.

200.description: The week. `targetValue: 0` means no goal is set — not an error.

get.description: The Home screen draws its three bars from this one call, so it returns a **bare array** in kcal / kg / km order. A member who has never set a training goal is seeded one first, from their weight goal and latest weighing — see the class comment for why that replaces legacy`s counseling answers.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/DD`; defaults to today (JST).

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Accepted and ignored — every unit is returned.

200.description: One entry per unit, always three.

get.summary: [legacy] All three units` weekly goal progress

get.description: The day`s five planned slots merged with everything the member recorded that day — body records, workouts, aerobic records, gate entries and exits, equipment usage — sorted by time. `targetCalories` is the **daily** target stored on this row, not the weekly kcal goal. A day never opened before is created by carrying the most recent earlier day forward with the completion flags reset, so the plan persists without being re-entered; a **future** day is shaped and returned with `id: null` rather than stored.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/DD`; defaults to today (JST).

200.description: The day, with its timeline.

get.summary: [legacy] The day`s plan, calorie target and merged timeline

patch.description: `activity` is **required** whenever `startTime`, `endTime` or `isCompleted` is present — without it there is no way to know which slot the values belong to. Editing **today`s** slot also pushes the new times onto every later day (flags and notes reset): the times are a routine, so a change to it applies going forward.

200.description: Legacy success message.

400.description: `targetCalories` on a past day or below zero, a slot edit on a future day, a slot field without `activity`, or a malformed date / time.

patch.summary: [legacy] Update the day`s calorie target and/or one planned slot

get.description:
One day: its rest-day flag and every routine/aerobic planned on it, newest first. The day row is created on first read, exactly as legacy did inside this GET — so a member who has never opened the Calendar still gets an `id` to PATCH.

An **aerobic** plan is matched to its record by legacy`s real plan→result foreign key: post `trainingScheduleId` on `POST /aerobic-records` and this plan reports `isCompleted: true` with that record`s id, title, duration and distance. A plan nothing claims falls back to the old derivation (any unclaimed record for the same aerobic master inside the JST day), which covers records written before migration 025 and the member who records first and plans afterwards.

A **routine** plan is still DERIVED — a session for the same routine inside the JST day. There the plan`s `scopeId` IS the session`s `routineId`, so the match holds; the only visible difference from legacy is that two plans for one routine on one day resolve to the same session, where legacy could tell them apart.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Omitted → today (JST), as in legacy.

200.description: The day, with its plans.

patch.description: Answers with legacy's `{message}`. The day is addressed by the `id` from `GET /schedules` (a UUID, like every other id in v2), not by date — legacy did the same, and a member cannot flag a day they have never read.

parameters.name: scheduleId
parameters.description: Day-row id (UUID) from `GET /schedules`.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: No such day row for the caller (E-SCH-001).

patch.summary: [legacy] Mark the day a rest day, or unmark it

post.description: Re-enters the create path, as legacy did — so the copy is re-validated and the target day's row is created if it does not exist yet. A plan whose routine has since been deleted is NOT copyable, matching legacy. Answers `{message}`; the new id is not returned (legacy did not return it either), so read the day back if you need it.

200.description: Legacy success message.

400.description: `trainingScheduleId` missing or not a UUID, or `date` malformed.

404.description: No such plan for the caller (E-SCH-002), or its routine/aerobic is gone (E-SCH-003).

post.summary: [legacy] Copy a plan onto another day

post.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.createAerobic`, the **first step of a three-call chain**: create the target → `POST /training-schedules` with its id as `scopeId` → (running flow) `POST /aerobic-records`. The path 404s on v2 today, so the whole chain is dead.

Legacy stored a per-member `aerobics` row holding `{targetDistance, targetDuration, type}` and returned it raw, with HTTP **200**. v2 has no per-member aerobic target table: planning points at an aerobic **master**. So `id` here is the master for the requested type — specifically the category placeholder (`AE-RUN-UNDEFINED` / `AE-BIKE-UNDEFINED`), the same row an aerobic record falls back to when it arrives without a machine, since the legacy target named no machine either. It is a preset, so `POST /training-schedules` accepts it as `scopeId` and the chain closes.

**The two target values are echoed back, not persisted.** The app uses them immediately (its calorie estimate) and that keeps working; re-reading the plan later still shows `duration: 0`, exactly as it does today — `GET /schedules` documents the same missing column. Storing them needs a migration and a product decision about whether v2 keeps per-member aerobic targets at all, so nothing is invented here.

**Still needs one FE change**: the app declares `AerobicResponse.id` as a `required int`, and every v2 id is a UUID string. A UUID into `required int` is a Dart `TypeError` — an `Error`, not an `Exception`, so it escapes the repository catch and breaks the screen. No backend shape can avoid that; the id has to round-trip to `scopeId`.

200.description: The legacy `Aerobics` entity shape (HTTP 200, as legacy).

400.description: `type` is not `running`/`bike`, or a target is not a positive number (E-VAL-001).

post.description:
Answers with the created row (`id`, `scheduleId`, `scopeId`, `scopeType`, timestamps) — legacy returned the raw entity and the app parses exactly those four fields.

`scopeId` must be a routine the caller owns or an official/HQ one, or an aerobic from the master (including their own custom ones); anything else is a 404 rather than a dangling plan. The day row is created only AFTER that check passes, so a bad `scopeId` leaves nothing behind.

Returns **200**, not 201: legacy forced `@HttpCode(HttpStatus.OK)` here.

200.description: The created plan row.

404.description: `scopeId` is not a routine/aerobic available to the caller (E-SCH-003).

post.summary: [legacy] Plan a routine or aerobic on a day

delete.description: Soft delete, as in legacy — the row stays for history and drops out of `GET /schedules`. Answers `{message}`.

parameters.name: trainingScheduleId
parameters.description: Plan id (UUID) from `GET /schedules`.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: No such plan for the caller, or already deleted (E-SCH-002).

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.getFolders`. A bare ARRAY, ordered by `position`, each folder listing its routines with the muscles their movements work.

Two legacy rules kept because the screen depends on them: a routine with **no movement** is dropped from `routines` AND from `routineCount`, so a freshly created empty routine is invisible here until a movement is added; and `coreMuscles` is filtered to the codes the app`s `MuscleEffect` can decode, since `exercises.primary_muscle` also holds the coarse API-003 category values.

The canonical `GET /routine-folders` answers a `{folders}` envelope with `sortOrder` and a count of every routine — same rows, different question.

200.description: The caller`s folders, ascending by `position`.

get.summary: [legacy] Folders with the routines inside them

post.description: Legacy answered with the folder alone — no `routineCount`, no `routines` (both are declared on its shared `FolderResponse` class but never filled by the create path). Backed by the canonical `CreateRoutineFolder`, so the folder still lands at `max(position) + 1`.

200.description: The created folder.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `RoutinesApiClient.getSystemRoutines`. The HQ masters (`routines.origin = official`) HQ has published in CRM Y-09, each with the caller`s own copy and the plan they already made for `date`.

`duplicateRoutineId` is found through `routines.source_routine_id` — the provenance column that `POST /v1/fitness-member/routines/{id}/duplicate` and the share path set on every copy. A copy made before those did (they used to leave it null) is not found here. `trainingScheduleId` is looked up against that copy, not the master: legacy planned the copy and reported the master it came from, so a master with no copy never has one.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Routine-category UUID. Omit for every category.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` for the `trainingScheduleId` lookup; defaults to today (JST).

200.description: The masters, newest first.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `RoutinesApiClient.getRoutineCategories`, which the Create-Training-Plan screen calls on open.

**This path was not merely missing — it was being answered by the wrong handler.** With no declaration of its own it fell through to `GET routines/:routineId` below, which ran `routine.findFirst({ id: "list-category" })` against a `@db.Uuid` column and returned a **500** (verified on dev). So the screen could not even see a clean 404 to fall back from. Declaring it HERE — above `:routineId` — is the whole fix; Nest matches in declaration order.

Same rows as the canonical `GET /api/v1/routine-categories` (API-130), which stays the path new code should call. Legacy returned `{id, name}` only; `description` is included because API-130 v0.2 added it and the app already has a slot for it under the banner.

200.description: Active routine categories, ordered by sortOrder.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.getWorkOutByDate`. A **bare array**, no envelope.

**No v2 spec and no legacy Swagger row** — legacy REMOVED this endpoint in Feb 2025 (`fix/calendar-workout-list`, commit `052a287a`), which is why it is absent from `fitness-api-swagger.json`. Its handler and service survive in git history, and that source plus the shipped client`s `WorkOutByDateResponse` are the whole contract. The app still declares the call.

Same rows as `GET /trainings/history`, narrowed to one day and **not** filtered by whether a post exists: this screen renders the post, the picker there excludes workouts that have one. `personal` is the field `trainings/history` calls `achieved` — the same 0…4 自己ベスト score, scored against the member`s whole history rather than the day`s.

`date` is optional and defaults to **today in JST**, as legacy defaulted to today; `YYYY/MM/DD` is accepted alongside `YYYY-MM-DD`, as legacy`s regex was. The day is a JST day, and a workout falls on the day of its `startedAt` — the date the timer owns and the calendar draws it on — not the row`s insert timestamp legacy had to use.

Legacy`s `name` is kept even though the shipped DTO drops it; its declared-but-never-sent `feed.images` IS populated, because that is the key the app reads.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY/MM/DD`. Defaults to today in JST.

200.description: The day`s workouts, newest first. Empty array when there are none.

get.summary: [legacy] One day`s workouts, each with the post about it — routines/workout-by-date

post.description:
Copies the routine into each target member`s library and answers legacy`s message. The routine may be the caller`s own or an HQ master, as in legacy — the master only while it is published in CRM Y-09.

A target that cannot receive the routine costs only itself — legacy used `Promise.allSettled` so one unreachable member did not fail the share, and that is kept. The response therefore does not tell the caller how many copies landed; legacy`s did not either.

Not carried over: legacy also pushed a `RoutineMenuShared` notification per target. That belongs to notification-svc and is left to the notification cluster rather than half-built here.

parameters.name: routineId
parameters.description: Routine to share. UUID in v2.

200.description: Legacy success message.

404.description: Routine not found, or neither the caller`s nor a master.

post.summary: [legacy] Share a routine with other members

post.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `RoutinesApiClient.completedTraining`. Writes the whole workout as one completed session — the call arrives with every set already in the body, so there is no session to start after the fact — and answers legacy`s summary. Legacy forced HTTP **200** here rather than 201; kept.

Sets are stored confirmed, so the same rows are what `GET /exercises/{id}/training-by-date` and API-015 history read back. Several sets of one movement share a single `session_exercises` row (it is unique per session+exercise) and are numbered within it.

`exerciseSetId` and `distanceMeters` are accepted and ignored: v2 records a set against the session rather than the routine`s template set, and `training_sets` has no distance column.

See the response schema for the two legacy quirks it reproduces (`description` carries the routine NAME, and `achieved` is measured against the member`s whole history).

200.description: The workout summary.

400.description: Body failed schema validation, or the plan is not the caller`s (E-VAL-001).

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.getTrainingResult`. The screen shown right after a workout — and the one Record Beginner lands on — read `{workoutMetrics}` from here; the path 404d on v2, so the screen had nothing to show.

Unlike its siblings this one needs no new RPC: it reads the session through the same `GetSession`/`GetAerobicSession` the canonical detail endpoints use and re-aggregates, which is also why the arithmetic lives in `legacy-calendar-body.ts` as pure functions rather than in training-svc.

`scopeId` is the SESSION id (what `POST /routines/completed` and `POST /aerobic-records` answer with), not the routine or the aerobic master — legacy`s `getMetricsResultTraining(trainingId)` was the same.

Two faithful details worth knowing: `totalExercises` counts DISTINCT movements, so a session that repeats one movement counts it once; and `volume` is recomputed as `Σ weight × reps` rather than read from the persisted total, which is what legacy`s `calculateDataTraining` did.

parameters.name: scopeId
parameters.description: Session UUID.

parameters.name: scopeType
parameters.description: Which session table to read.

200.description: The session`s metrics.

400.description: `scopeId` missing or `scopeType` not one of the two (E-VAL-001).

404.description: No such session for the caller.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.getFeeds`. Returns the legacy `FeedResponseDto[]` — **a bare array, not a pagination envelope** — with offset paging, because that is what the shipped client sends and reads.

Backed by the social-svc `GetLegacyFeed` RPC rather than `GET /api/v1/social-feed`: the legacy query is a different query, not a different envelope. It unions the requested `shareScope` values, always includes the caller's own posts at any visibility (legacy's base clause), and carries the per-card data the canonical feed drops — the full media list (canonical returns a thumbnail plus a count), the follow direction both ways, the liker avatars, and the workout/aerobic detail.

**One mapping is lossy:**
• `shareScope=suggest` is folded into `public`: legacy selected store-mates' posts, and the contract/favourite stores live outside social-svc (the same blocker as the Likes-List row). With `public` also requested — the app's default — nothing is lost.

`shareScopes` **and** `shareScope` are both returned: legacy's service emitted the plural while its DTO declared the singular, and the app reads the plural.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Defaults to 5 (legacy `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE_FEED`); capped at 50.

parameters.name: shareScope
parameters.description: Legacy `QueryFeedEnum`; repeatable. The app sends all three.

200.description: Feed cards, newest first.

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

post.description:
Compat endpoint for the mobile `FeedsApiClient.createFeed`. **Images are uploaded before the post, not with it**: `POST /api/v1/media/presign` with tag `social-media` → `PUT` the bytes to the returned URL with its `requiredHeaders` → send the returned `s3Key`s here as `feedFiles`. That is the one agreed upload flow, shared with the canonical `POST /api/v1/members/me/social-posts`.

**This replaces the multipart form the shipped (old) app sent.** Legacy accepted the binaries on this call; the new client uploads first and sends keys, which is also what legacy's own `CreateFeedDto` declared (`feedFiles?: string[]`). At most 4 files, and social-svc caps them at 3 images and 1 video (legacy took 4 images; the app's picker stops at 3).

**The attached record is checked the way legacy checked it.** A `trainingId` must be the caller's workout and not yet posted about (social-svc). An `aerobicRecordId` must be the caller's aerobic record and not yet posted about — checked here, because the canonical contract validates only the workout ref — and the post is dated with the record's own date. Either id must be a UUID.

`shareScope` maps onto `visibility` (`public`→`everyone`, `onlyFollower`→`followers_only`, `onlyMe`→`self_only`) and `caption` onto the post body. No `title` is sent: v2 date-stamps one, as the legacy create did.

Returns legacy's `{message}` and **201**.

201.description: Post created; legacy message returned.

400.description: `shareScope` missing/unknown, more than 4 `feedFiles`, or `trainingId` / `aerobicRecordId` not a UUID (E-VAL-001).

post.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.postFeedAction`. Routes the legacy `?actionType=` to the v2 endpoint that now owns it: `POST /api/v1/follows`, `POST /api/v1/mutes`, `POST /api/v1/blocks`.

Follows are created as `followType: follow`; the coach flavour has no legacy counterpart. Blocking in v2 tears down the follow edges in **both** directions and the mutes both ways (BR-SOC-019). Legacy soft-deleted only the blocker's own follow of the target; the target's follow of the blocker survived the block (and so an unblock).

Repeating an action is **success, not a conflict**: legacy returned its message when the row already existed, so v2's 409 (`E-SNS-042`/`047`/`048`) is swallowed here.

Returns legacy's `{message}` and **201**, as fitness-api did.

parameters.name: targetMemberId
parameters.description: Target member **UUID** (the app still declares an int).

parameters.name: actionType
parameters.description: Legacy `SnsActionEnum`.

201.description: Relationship written; legacy message returned.

400.description: `actionType` missing or not one of `follow`/`mute`/`block`, or `targetMemberId` not a UUID (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

404.description: Target member not found or withdrawn (E-SNS-040).

422.description: Target is the caller (E-SNS-045), or — `follow` only — a block stands between the two members (E-SNS-041).

delete.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.deleteFeedAction`. Routes the legacy `?actionType=` to `DELETE /api/v1/mutes/{memberId}` / `DELETE /api/v1/blocks/{memberId}`, and for `follow` to the social-svc `DeleteFollowByTarget` RPC — the canonical `DELETE /api/v1/follows/{followId}` needs a follow id the app never receives.

**Idempotent**: removing something that is not there is a 200 here, where legacy threw a bare 400. Unblocking does **not** restore the follows the block tore down (BR-SOC-019). Legacy did not restore the blocker's follow either, but it had never removed the target's follow of the blocker, which v2 does — so that one is gone after an unblock here and was not in legacy.

Returns legacy's `{message}` and **200**.

parameters.name: targetMemberId
parameters.description: Target member **UUID** (the app still declares an int).

parameters.name: actionType
parameters.description: Legacy `SnsActionEnum`.

post.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.postReports`. Delegates to `POST /api/v1/user-reports` (API-043) with `reportMemberId` → `targetMemberId` and `reportContent` → `detail`.

v2 requires a `reason` category that the legacy contract has no field for; it defaults to `spam` and can be overridden by sending `reason` in the body. **TODO(upstream)**: API-043 has no `other` value, which is what this default really wants.

Returns legacy's `{message}`; the v2 report id is deliberately not surfaced (legacy never had it).

201.description: Report filed; legacy message returned.

400.description: `reportMemberId` blank or not a UUID, or `reportContent` blank/over 300 characters (E-VAL-001).

404.description: Target member not found or inactive (E-SNS-040).

422.description: Cannot report yourself (E-SNS-045).

post.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.postReaction`. Delegates to `POST /api/v1/social-posts/{postId}/reactions` (API-036) with the post id moved from the body to the path.

The legacy emotion axis is gone: `like`/`love`/`care`/`haha`/`wow`/`sad` all map to v2 `like`, because v2 models reactions as one like plus stamp codes (BR-SOC-011). The shipped app only ever sends `love`, so **calling the v2 endpoint directly with `love` is a 422** — that mapping is the point of this facade. A v2 stamp code passes through unchanged.

Legacy forced **200** on this POST (not 201) and swallowed v2's idempotency signal, so a repeat like is a 200 here too.

200.description: Reaction written (or already present); legacy message returned.

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

404.description: Post not found / deleted / not viewable (E-SNS-004).

422.description: Reaction type is neither a legacy emotion nor a v2 stamp code (E-SNS-010).

delete.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.deleteReaction`. The legacy call carries **no reaction type** — it held one row per (member, post) and deleted whatever was there — while the canonical `DELETE /api/v1/social-posts/{postId}/reactions/{reactionType}` needs one. So this goes to the social-svc `RemoveAllReactions` RPC, which drops every reaction of the caller on that post (a like *and* any stamps, which v2 allows together).

**Idempotent**: no reaction to remove is still a 200, as legacy's soft delete of zero rows was.

Returns legacy's `{message}` and **200**.

parameters.name: feedId
parameters.description: Post **UUID** (the app still declares an int).

200.description: Reaction removed (or none was present); legacy message returned.

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.getComments`. Comments **oldest first**, as legacy ordered them — the Comment Page appends new ones at the bottom, so the order is load-bearing.

⚠️ **This deviates from the v2 spec deliberately.** APP-D-01 FR-M006 ("Text replies are not possible"), BR-SOC-011 and API-036 §Rejected Alternatives all rejected text comments in favour of stamps, so v2 had no table for them. The shipped client still has a Comment Page, and the decision was to build the legacy contract and carry the deviation as errata. Stamps remain a separate axis on `POST /feeds/reactions`.

Authors in a block relation with the caller are hidden. Legacy filtered one direction only (members the caller had blocked); this is symmetric, matching every other social read — it only ever hides more.

The post itself must be one the caller may view, as for reactions: a `self_only` post, a `followers_only` post the caller does not follow, a deleted one or one across a block answers the same empty page as a UUID that is no post (legacy checked none of this).

parameters.name: feedId
parameters.description: Post **UUID** (the app still declares an int).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Defaults to 50 (legacy `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`); capped at 100.

200.description: Comments, oldest first.

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

post.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.comment`. Returns the created comment (legacy `CommentResponseDto`) and **201**.

Same spec deviation as the list above — see it for the FR references.

The post must be one the caller may view — the rule the list and reactions apply. Every way of failing it (no such post, deleted, out of reach by visibility, a block in either direction) is the one `400 E-VAL-001`, so the answer does not reveal which. Legacy answered a bare 400 when the author had blocked you (and a 422 from its validator for a missing post). The block test used to be one-directional as legacy's was, but this list filters blocks both ways, so a member who had blocked the author could post a comment the author would never see.

201.description: The created comment.

400.description: `feedId` missing or not a UUID, `content` missing/empty, or no post the caller may comment on (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `FeedsApiClient.getMembersRelationships` **and** `MyPageApiClient`'s follower/following lists. One legacy endpoint multiplexes four different queries behind `?type=`, all answering the same `{data, hasNextPage, total}` envelope:

• `reaction` — who reacted to one post (the Likes List screen). **`feedId` is required.**
• `suggest` — members to follow from the caller's own gym (the feed's filter sheet).
• `following` / `follower` — My Page's two lists; `targetMemberId` views somebody else's.

All four are implemented, not just the two Feed rows: the app calls this one path from both screens, so answering half of them with a validation error would be worse than the 404 this replaces.

`status` is always relative to **the caller**, never to the list's owner — browsing another member's followers, each row says what your own follow button should do.

⚠️ **`suggest` is narrower than legacy.** Legacy matched a favourite store OR a contract store; v2 has no favourite-store table anywhere, so only the contract store (`members.primary_store_id`) can be matched. A member who only favourited a gym they have no contract with sees fewer suggestions than legacy gave them. Random order and a cap of 10 are legacy's own.

`reaction` counts **distinct members**: v2 lets one member leave a like *and* several stamps on a post where legacy held one row per member, so without that a single reactor would appear repeatedly and inflate `total`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Legacy `MemberRelationshipEnum`.

parameters.name: feedId
parameters.description: Post **UUID**. Required when `type=reaction`.

parameters.name: targetMemberId
parameters.description: Member **UUID** whose list to view. `following`/`follower` only; defaults to the caller.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Defaults to 1.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Defaults to 50 (legacy `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE`); capped at 100.

200.description: The matching members, newest relation first.

400.description: `type` missing or unknown, `type=reaction` without a UUID `feedId`, or a `targetMemberId` that is not a UUID (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

get.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.getTrainingsHistory`. Feeds the workout picker on the Create Post screen: the member's sessions **that have not been posted about yet**, in the legacy `ListRoutineResponDTO` shape — a bare array, no envelope.

Legacy did that exclusion with `feed: { id: IsNull() }`, a join it could make in one query because feeds and trainings shared a database. `training_session_id` now lives in social-svc, so the two reads run in parallel and the posted ids are dropped here. Deleting a post frees its workout again, as it did in legacy.

`achieved` is legacy's 自己ベスト score: how many of the four metrics — max weight, reps, volume, estimated 1RM — this workout holds for the member. **0…4, counting metrics, not exercises**; a first-ever workout scores 4, because legacy compared against a history that already included the session. `description` repeats `name` (legacy assigned the routine's *name* to it), and legacy's declared-but-never-populated `image` is absent.

Ordering is newest-first. Legacy issued no ORDER BY at all, which is not a contract; its lack of a LIMIT is kept, since the picker has no paging and capping it would hide older workouts.

200.description: Workouts not yet attached to a post, newest first.

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

get.summary: [legacy] Workouts available to post about — trainings/history

patch.description:
Compat endpoint matching the mobile `TrainingApiClient.updateTraining`. It belongs to the Create Post screen, not to My Page: the beginner-mode record-post flow fires it **in parallel with `POST /feeds`** and treats either failure as a failed post, so while this route was missing that screen reported an error even though the post had been created.

**Not the same operation as `PATCH /api/v1/training-sessions/{sessionId}`** (that one ends a session — complete/abandon) nor as `.../duration` (API-019's calorie-recalculating edit, which rejects a session that is not completed and hard-fails without a registered body weight). Legacy applied neither gate, and neither is applied here: the post screen cannot fix a missing body weight, so a duration change without one is stored and the calorie total is simply left as it was.

`title` is a new column on the session (migration 024) — v2 had no place for one, because a session is labelled by the routine it came from and a quick-start session had nothing to name.

Legacy's third optional field, `recordTime`, is **not accepted**: it moved the workout's own date, which in v2 is the session `startedAt` that the timer owns and the calendar, stats and feed all read. No shipped client sends it.

An empty body is a 200 with the legacy message, as it was in legacy, and a `null` field counts as not sent (legacy's `@IsOptional()`; the app's `toJson` always writes both keys). Returns `{message}`.

parameters.name: trainingId
parameters.description: Training session **UUID** (the app still declares an int).

200.description: Session updated; legacy message returned.

400.description: `trainingId` not a UUID, `title` empty or over 255 characters, or `duration` not an integer in 0…86399 (E-VAL-001).

403.description: Type C member (E-AUTH-100) — only on the routes social-svc gates: `GET`/`POST feeds`, `POST reports` and `POST`/`DELETE feeds/reactions`. Follow / mute / block, comments, `members/relationships` and the `trainings` routes carry no member-type gate.

404.description: No such session, or it belongs to another member — legacy conflated the two (E-EXR-002).

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `PayUnpaidApiClient.getUnpaidInfo` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/sales/uncollected-amount`) — the 未収 banner on Home and the Pay-Unpaid screen.

Thin rename over the canonical `GET /api/v1/members/me/uncollected-amount`: `amount` → `uncollectedAmount` and `billingIds` → `saleIds`, the latter passed through as **UUID strings** (ADR-038 D8). Those ids are what the pay endpoint needs back, so they are forwarded rather than dropped.

200.description: Legacy `{ uncollectedAmount, saleIds }`. `uncollectedAmount: 0` when nothing is owed — not a 404.

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `EntriesApiClient.getStampStreakLog` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/entries/streak-entry/{brand}`) — the stamp card on Home.

Computed the way fitness-api did, from the member's **gate visit days** (API-137 EP2): a card is ten distinct JST visit days. `streakLog` is the open card's days (`YYYY-MM-DD`, newest first) — or, on the day a card closes, that card's ten days; `total` is how many cards have closed; `completedAt` is when the newest one closed (the first entry of its tenth day).

`brand` is accepted and **ignored**: visit days are the member's own, whatever the brand.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Sent by the shipped app; **ignored** — the card is scoped to the member.

200.description: Legacy `{ streakLog, total, completedAt }`.

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `MembersApiClient.getMemberQrCode` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/members/qr-code`) — the QR the member shows at the gate.

The canonical route is `POST /api/v1/members/me/gate-qr` (API-054): both the **verb** and the field name changed, so a path alias was not enough. `qrPayload` → `qrCode`; `expiresAt` and `ttlSeconds` are dropped because legacy never sent them and the app reads neither.

**This GET has a side effect** — issuing a QR invalidates the member's previous token, so only the newest one opens the gate. Do not cache it, and do not pre-fetch it.

200.description: Legacy `{ qrCode }`. Short-lived and single-use — request a new one each time the screen opens.

403.description: Member not eligible for gate entry — Type C / inactive (E-AUTH-100).

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `LockersApiClient.getListLocker` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/lockers?storeId&optionId`) — the cabinet picker on Change Plan and Digital Ticket.

**Replaces the previous flat-slot answer.** This route used to return the canonical slot list under `lockers`, which was the wrong grain: legacy described the *cabinet* (area letter, photo, floor-map placement) and the app renders one tile per cabinet, then calls `lockers/lockers-slot?lockerId=` for the slots inside. `gymMapImage` is now the store's real floor plan instead of a hardcoded null.

`optionId` filters to cabinets carrying that option — a cabinet can hold two (a standard and a bottom-row fee), and either one matching keeps it.

⚠️ `longitude`/`latitude` are floor-map fractions `0.0–1.0`, not pixels — see the field descriptions before positioning anything with them.

parameters.name: storeId
parameters.description: Store **UUID**.

parameters.name: optionId
parameters.description: Keep only cabinets carrying this option **UUID**.

200.description: Legacy `{ gymMapImage, lockers }`.

get.summary: Legacy locker cabinets for a store (LockersReturnResponse)

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `GymApiClient.getMemberFamilyDetail` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/options/by-member-family?memberId=`) — the Family Detail screen.

**Answers a bare `{}`, not a 403, when the caller is not the queried member's parent.** That is legacy's behaviour and it is the safer one: it does not disclose whether the member exists or which household they belong to. The caller must be the householder and the target must be someone else in the same household.

`contract` is the plan line and `options` the active monthly options, both from the same source as `plan-options/me`. `fee` is **tax-inclusive**, as legacy's was (`contract.fee` / `option.fee` were 「料金(税込)」; the v2 master is 税込 too, so it is passed through — API-085 v0.12). `description` is always null — legacy declared it and never filled it.

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description: Household member **UUID**.

200.description: Legacy `OptionByMemberResponse`, or a bare `{}` when not permitted / not found.

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `GymApiClient.getListOptionOnceTime` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/options-once-time`). Rebuilt from fitness-api `getListOptionOnceTimeMe`: a ticket is a per-use option contract (`payment_type = per_use`, fitness-api `once`) on one of the seven kinds, still unused. Grouped per option, ascending option id; `count` tickets, `memberContractId` = the oldest (used first). `[]` when the member has none — the normal answer.

Tickets are only ever the caller's own (legacy did the same here). They are bought through `POST /api/v1/fitness-member/payment`; the option lists the app buys from offer per-use options of these seven kinds only, so every ticket bought there shows here.

200.description: Unused tickets per option; `[]` when none.

get.summary: Legacy digital tickets (チケット) — the caller's unused tickets, one entry per option

post.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `GymApiClient.activateDigitalTicket` (`POST /v1/fitness-member/options-once-time/activate`); the app treats 200/201 as success and ignores the body. The ticket goes `active → used` with `end_date` = today (JST) — the lifecycle contracts.dbml defines for 1Day / 1Time passes — so it drops out of `GET options-once-time`.

The app calls this only for protein / supplement tickets, right after the QR lookup (`GET protein/verify`, board STT 69) succeeds. Differences from legacy: only the caller's own ticket (legacy also accepted a family parent's, unchecked), and catalogued refusals where legacy answered a bare 400 — not the caller's ticket or not a ticket → 404 E-OPT-004; already used → 409 E-OPT-006. Answers legacy's `{ message }`.

201.description: Used. fitness-api's message, verbatim.

404.description: Not the caller's ticket, or not a ticket (E-OPT-004).

409.description: The ticket is already used, or changed meanwhile (E-OPT-006).

post.summary: Legacy digital ticket use — marks one of the caller's tickets used

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `GET /v1/fitness-member/protein/verify?name=&paymentType=&optionId=`. Rebuilt from fitness-api `verifyOptionProtein`, which did NOT call the vendor: it checked the caller holds the option and answered the QR payload.

**The check** (`name` = `Protein` | `Supplement` → `options.subcategory` `protein` | `supplement`):
- `paymentType=monthly` (default) — a live monthly option of that kind (active, or cancelled at month end and not yet ended). With `optionId`, it must be that option.
- `paymentType=once` — an unused per-use ticket of `optionId` (required; the `id` of a `GET options-once-time` entry). Nothing is used up here: the app calls `options-once-time/activate` afterwards.
- `paymentType=yearly` — accepted as legacy did; v2 has no yearly option, so always 404.

**`uniqueId`** = `9999` + the digits of the member number, zero-padded to 10 (legacy: `9999` + `members.id`).

**Monthly — vendor registration gate** (protein: meeting workflow 2026-11-05; supplement: "Supplyment FLow"): the protein (alight) and supplement (GRANDE) machines ask their VENDOR's server, so the QR is answered only once BAT-PROTEIN-SYNC / BAT-SUPPLEMENT-SYNC has registered the member there and the period the vendor accepted covers today; `uniqueId` is then the code it was registered under. Holding the option but not registered yet (just bought — the batches run every 5 minutes — or the registration failed) → 409 E-OPT-005, and the app shows no QR. Per-use tickets are not registered with a vendor and are not gated.

Differences from legacy: only the caller's own contracts count (legacy also accepted a family parent's option flagged family-usable; v2 options have no such flag), and the refusal is the catalogued E-OPT-004 rather than a bare 404.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Default `Protein`.

parameters.name: paymentType
parameters.description: Default `monthly`.

parameters.name: optionId
parameters.description: Option **UUID** (legacy int). Required when `paymentType=once`.

200.description: The caller holds the option; the QR payload.

400.description: Unknown `name` / `paymentType`, `optionId` missing (once) or not a UUID, or `optionId` is a ticket of another kind (E-VAL-001).

404.description: The caller holds no such option / unused ticket (E-OPT-004).

409.description: Monthly: the option is held but the member is not (yet) registered on the vendor server for today (E-OPT-005).

get.summary: Legacy protein / supplement QR — the code the vendor machine reads (board STT 69)

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `GymApiClient.getTicketsOnePass` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/tickets-one-pass?page=&limit=`). Rebuilt from fitness-api `getTicketOnePassMemberContract`: every 1Day pass of the caller (ended ones too), newest first, with its tickets counted — used, expired (unused past the last day), remaining — and the unused ticket that expires first. A ticket is valid 180 days from purchase. `status` is `using` while a ticket of the pass was activated today (JST).

⚠ ids are UUIDs; the shipped app declares `id` / `nextExpiringTicket.id` / `memberContractId` as `int` (TypeError until it switches to String).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Legacy default 5; the app sends 10000.

200.description: Passes, newest first. `data: []` when the member holds no 1Day pass.

get.summary: Legacy 1Day tickets (チケット画面) — the caller's 1Day passes with their ticket counts (board STT 89)

patch.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `GymApiClient.useTicket` (`PATCH /v1/fitness-member/tickets-one-pass/activate/{memberContractId}`, `HttpResponse<String>`). Takes the unused, unexpired ticket of the pass that expires first and marks it used today (JST). For the rest of that day the gate admits the member — at the pass's own store only — and the pass reads `using`. The body (`usageStartDate`) is ignored.

Differences from legacy: a second call the same day does NOT take another ticket (legacy did; the app retries a failed call up to 3 times) and answers the same success; the body is **text/plain** — the app reads it as a String, and legacy's JSON object made the app report an error after the ticket was already used.

parameters.name: memberContractId
parameters.description: The pass `id` from `GET tickets-one-pass`.

200.description: fitness-api's message, as plain text.

schema.example: アップデートは成功しました

400.description: Not a UUID (E-VAL-001), or no unused ticket left on the pass (E-CTR-203).

404.description: Not a live 1Day pass of the caller (E-CTR-202).

patch.summary: Legacy 1Day ticket use (使用する) — activates today's ticket of one pass (board STT 90)

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `StoreApiClient.checkTransferStore` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/transfers/store?storeId=`) — the Request Transfer and Confirm Contract screens.

Renames the canonical API-142 application onto legacy's keys (`transferApplicationId`→`id`, `fromStoreId`→`sourceStoreId`, `toStoreId`→`destinationStoreId`, `reasonCode`→`transferReason`) and **maps the status down to `transferProcessing`** — see the field description; passing v2's value through blanks the screen silently.

Answers a bare `{}` when there is no transfer in flight, as legacy did. `storeId` filters to a transfer leaving that store, matching legacy; omit it to get whichever is open.

parameters.name: storeId
parameters.description: Keep the application only if it leaves this store **UUID** — legacy filtered on it.

200.description: Legacy's transfer shape, or a bare `{}` when none is in flight.

post.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `StoreApiClient.transferStore` (`POST /v1/fitness-member/transfers/store`) — the Request Transfer screen's submit. Files the canonical API-142 EP-B application, so every rule is the canonical one (brand, same store, in-flight transfer / withdrawal, delinquency).

The body is **mapped**, per API-142 §11.4: `destinationStoreId` → `toStoreId`; the legacy free-text `transferReason` → `reasonCode: "other"` + `reasonDetail` (first 500 characters) — the app has no reason-code picker, it joins checkbox labels; `scheduledTransferDate` → the JST calendar day. `sourceContractId` / `sourceStoreId` are ignored: 移籍元 is the caller's main contract (§3.2).

Answers legacy's `{ message }` (the app declares `Future<void>`), with the v2 application id where legacy put its int id.

That is why this is not the canonical API-142 EP-C as-is: EP-C always answers `200 { verifiable, blockers }`, so an ineligible transfer would read as "go ahead". This runs EP-C and, like legacy, **fails when the transfer is not allowed** — with the first blocker's catalogued code and status (E-STR-001 404, E-TRF-006 409, E-TRF-008 / E-MEM-205 / E-TRF-009 422).

`storeId` and `contractId` are accepted and ignored (the source is the caller's main contract, and a transfer keeps the plan).

Compat path matching the shipped mobile `SalesApiClient.createPenaltySales` (`POST /v1/fitness-member/sales/create-penalty-sales`), called by the app right after the 退会 application is filed. Bills the penalty of the requested campaigns as one withdrawal invoice (`penalty_recovery` lines) and charges the card on file at once, as legacy did.

Not legacy's trust model: the penalty is recomputed for today (JST) — `saleDetailIds`, `storeId` and `salesMonth` are ignored, `campaignId` only selects — and the member must have an open 退会 application (404 E-WDR-001). One invoice per application: a repeat call answers 200 without billing or charging again. `penaltyDatas: []` (the app sends it when the estimate was empty), or nothing due any more, is 200 with nothing charged.

post.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `MemberContractsApiClient.estimateChangePlanOptionFee` (`POST /v1/fitness-member/checkout/change-plan-options`), also used by the digital-ticket checkout. Nothing is written. Rebuilt from fitness-api `checkoutChangePlanOption`: a plan change (`contractId` → `contractChangeId`) needs a plan sold at the contract's store and the current plan's 主契約変更可否; `optionDeleteIds` are option ids the member holds now; `optionNewIds` must be sold at the store. An option already booked for next month (`isOptionAdd`) sent again in `optionNewIds` is left out — not refused, not listed, not priced (legacy took it). A locker is priced like any monthly option; its `lockerSlotId` is optional here and checked when sent.

`billPaymentNow` prices only the `payNow` options: a monthly option prorated for the rest of the month (when the option says so), a one-time option in full × `quantity`; lines 税抜, tax per rate. The v2 master is 税込 like legacy's (API-085 v0.12), so legacy's steps run on the stored value.

200.description: Legacy's ConfirmChangeOptionsPlanResponse.

400.description: Bad ids, an id twice, a quantity out of range, a store other than the contract's — allowed only for a ticket-only purchase (E-VAL-001).

404.description: No live contract (E-CTR-202); target plan not sold here (E-PLN-001); option not sold here (E-OPT-001); not one of the member's options (E-OPT-004); locker slot not found at the contract's store (E-LOC-002).

409.description: Plan not changeable / same plan (E-CTR-200); option already held — one only booked for next month is skipped instead (E-OPT-005); locker slot not free (E-LOC-008).

422.description: Option not addable (E-OPT-010); a one-time option not `payNow`, a slot on a non-locker option or a slot priced by another option (E-OPT-007); the contract already holds a locker slot, or a second locker in one request (E-LOC-009).

post.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `POST /v1/fitness-member/payment` from the Change Plan screen and the digital-ticket purchase. Legacy `modifyMemberContracts`:
• `upgradeContractId` (+ `contractId`) → a plan change applied from the 1st of next month (BAT-018); the plan a change is already booked to, sent again with an option change, stays booked (not booked twice) and the options apply;
• `addOptionIds` → `payNow` options start today and are charged NOW to the card on file (a monthly one prorated and then billed monthly from next month; one-time tickets × `quantity`); others start the 1st of next month; an option already booked for next month, sent again, stays booked once (not booked or charged twice);
• `memberContractIds` → options cancelled at the end of this month (one not yet started: at once); one already ending this month (`isOptionCancel`) has its cancel taken back — the app's 取り消し sends the same id again, as legacy toggled `cancelFlag` — and is `active` again.
• a locker in `addOptionIds` carries its `lockerSlotId` (required): the slot is taken (API-101) in the same transaction as the option contract, even for a next-month locker; one cancelled before it starts frees it.

Differences from legacy: everything is validated before anything is charged or written, and written in one transaction; a declined card writes nothing (E-EXT-011 / no card E-CARD-001); only the member's own cancel made here can be taken back, and only before its end date (one by staff, a locker release or a store transfer → E-OPT-006), under the add guards since the option goes on being billed; the same id within 30 seconds of the member's own cancel / take-back is the app retrying it and changes nothing (legacy's toggle undid a retried cancel); only the caller's own options can be cancelled; API-094's member guards apply (休会/退会 states E-OPT-005, arrears E-MEM-205); the same body again within 10 minutes is the same request (the app retries a 5xx) and is not charged twice — for a body that buys a ticket, within 30 seconds only (after 60 seconds the same ticket × quantity is always a new purchase); a locker slot must be free (legacy's next-month add never marked it taken) and a contract holds one slot, so a second locker or a swap in one request is refused (E-LOC-009).

`sbps_link` answers an HTML page for the app's WebView (legacy did) that forwards to `ok_return_url` after the charge; only `linkType: credit` (the card on file) is supported. Otherwise 201 with an empty body (legacy).

201.description: Applied. Empty body; `sbps_link` → an HTML page (string).

400.description: Bad ids / quantity / store / linkType, or a locker without `lockerSlotId` (E-VAL-001).

404.description: E-CTR-202 / E-PLN-001 / E-OPT-001 / E-OPT-004 / locker slot not found (E-LOC-002), or no card on file (E-CARD-001).

409.description: Plan not changeable or a change to another plan already booked (E-CTR-200); option held / member state (E-OPT-005); a cancel that cannot be taken back — not the member's own, or past its end date (E-OPT-006); locker slot not free (E-LOC-008).

422.description: Arrears (E-MEM-205), option not addable (E-OPT-010 / E-OPT-007), the contract already holds a locker slot (E-LOC-009).

Compat path matching the shipped mobile `RestApiPath.getPointExternal` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/point/external/get_point`), which backs both point screens and the member rank.

**Not an alias of `GET /api/v1/points/balance`.** That endpoint reports one number; legacy reported the Yamauchi shape — a `balance` array and a `cumuluses` array keyed by payment type — and the app reads the `point` entry of each. This returns a single-entry array per side, filled from the v2 ledger: `available` is the spendable balance and `total` is lifetime **earned**, which is what the rank thresholds are defined against.

`memberId` and `brand` are accepted and **ignored** — the caller is the JWT subject and the brand is theirs. Reads are brand-isolated (BR-PNT-007) but **not brand-gated**: ENJOY (JOYFIT) points are in launch scope since TBD-007 closed 2026-08-06, so a JOYFIT member is answered from the ledger like anyone else. Zeros mean an empty ledger, not a blocked brand.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Sent by the shipped app; **ignored** (the brand comes from the member's own record).

parameters.name: memberId
parameters.description: Sent by the shipped app; **ignored** (the member is the JWT subject).

**Nothing to register in v2**: the point server is the internal `point_transactions` ledger (API-155, BAT-064 §1.1), which needs no member record before points are awarded or read. So this answers the external server's success envelope and changes nothing. The body is accepted and **ignored** — the member is the JWT subject, as for `external/get_point`.

`totalPoints` counts **earned** points only, and `month` is `YY-MM` with a **two-digit year** — both are legacy behaviours the app depends on; see the field descriptions before "correcting" either.

**`month` is `YYYY-MM` here while `monthlies` returns `YY-MM`.** That asymmetry is legacy's and it is load-bearing: the app converts between the two (`DateTime(2000 + YY, MM)` → `yyyy-MM`), so matching the formats up would break the round trip. Months are cut in JST.

get.description:
Compat path matching the shipped mobile `PointApiClient.getLatestReward` (`GET /v1/fitness-member/point/latest-reward`) — the "+N ポイント" popup on Home and after a workout. **No canonical counterpart**: API-045 paginates history, it does not answer "the newest award matching these scopes".

Answers a bare `{}` when nothing matches, exactly as legacy's `result ?? {}` did — the app reads that as "no popup", so it is the normal empty answer, not an error.

`scopeType` is legacy vocabulary for *what the points were for* and is mapped from the v2 `eventType`; a filter that maps to nothing (e.g. `stamp` alone, which is not a ledger row) matches nothing rather than falling through to "unfiltered".

parameters.name: startTime
parameters.description: Only awards created strictly after this instant. A date-time **without an offset is read as JST** — the app sends local midnight that way, and fitness-api ran in Asia/Tokyo. `Z`/offsets are honoured.

parameters.name: scopeType
parameters.description: Legacy scope names; repeatable. Omitted = any scope.
